[1386] IN FUTURE NORWEGIAN

[1387] The strategic situation in Europe has fundamentally changed since the end of the Cold War, and the security situation in our immediate vicinity is currently positive

[1388] The Government will work actively to further improve this situation, not least by contributing to international peace and stability in a broad sense

[1389] However, we have no guarantee that new conflicts will not arise

[1390] The Government therefore sees it as necessary to have available and relevant instruments to meet a number of security policy challenges that vary in terms of their proximity in time, likelihood of occurrence, and consequences if they occur

[1391] These instruments primarily include modern military forces that can both secure national sovereignty and enable Norway to contribute to preventing and resolving international conflicts

[1392] Due to the changed geostrategic and international situation, Norway is receiving less attention from our allies than before

[1393] At the same time, we, as a wealthy country, are expected to shoulder our share of the burdens through participation in joint defense and international peacekeeping operations

[1394] In this context, it cannot be ruled out that NATO or coalitions of NATO countries will become more involved in peace operations outside Europe as well

[1395] To contribute to continued stability and to ensure the necessary support in connection with future challenges, we must use a broad range of security policy instruments

[1396] The future will therefore require more resources and strengthened expertise in a broader field than before

[1397] That is not the same as saying that everything is equally important

[1398] The government's main task is to ensure our national and territorial security and sovereignty, but at the same time a number of other tasks must be taken care of

[1399] It is therefore important that security and defense policy is planned and designed from a holistic and long-term perspective

[1400] With this as a starting point, the defence policy goals and the Defence's tasks will be presented in chapter

[1401] The risk dimension and the alliance dimension

[1402] The government's security policy is based on two fundamental dimensions: the risk dimension and the alliance dimension

[1403] The risk dimension encompasses the spectrum of security challenges and applies to everything from the danger of violation of Norwegian sovereignty to crises, military attacks or attacks

[1404] War that affects one's own territory and population will have by far the worst consequences

[1405] In the foreseeable future, this risk dimension will be linked to the significant conventional and nuclear military capabilities located in our immediate vicinity

[1406] As described earlier, there is currently no military threat from Russia, and the government places great emphasis on further developing security and defense policy cooperation with Russia

[1407] However, the bilateral relationship is also characterized by an unclear border division in an area of great military and, not least, resource importance, and with an important and vulnerable maritime environment

[1408] Regardless of development, the bilateral relationship will always be characterized by the asymmetrical power relationship between a great power and a small state

[1409] The risk posed by Russian military capabilities is primarily related to the uncertain internal developments in Russia and the danger of armed conflicts spreading from other regions to our neighboring areas

[1410] Russia faces a number of long-term challenges of an economic, social, political and security nature, and has an unclear relationship with several of its neighboring countries

[1411] A number of potential conflicts and conflicts of interest exist along the borders in the south and east

[1412] These are, among other things, linked to religious and ethnic minorities and to the exploitation and control of natural resources

[1413] But even though Russia will continue to have major economic problems, the country also has very large resources in a number of areas and great potential for further economic growth and development

[1414] The risk dimension also includes other types of dangers such as the spread of nuclear, biological and chemical weapons, terrorist attacks and environmental disasters

[1415] The best possible protection of our military forces abroad, for example against the possible use of weapons of mass destruction, will also have greater importance for our planning

[1416] The alliance dimension is naturally linked to the risk dimension

[1417] Norway will continue to depend on NATO cooperation to be able to handle major crises and military attacks

[1418] and our defense planning will continue to be based on membership in the alliance

[1419] But there is also a certain uncertainty associated with this dimension, that is, with the future development of NATO, both as a military alliance and as a political consultation forum

[1420] We have no guarantee that this development will be in accordance with Norwegian interests or our emphasis on various risks

[1421] Both the United States and European allies have identified possible force contributions to Norway in the event of a crisis or conflict

[1422] NATO has increasingly moved away from a structure with specifically earmarked forces

[1423] The trend is rather towards flexible solutions, with most NATO countries developing mobile military units and force packages with multiple deployment options

[1424] For Norway, it will be a challenge to ensure that these military units and force packages can also have Norway as a deployment option

[1425] This requires continued emphasis on cooperation with the United States

[1426] In addition, it will require increased emphasis on cooperation with the most important European allies

[1427] Reduced defense budgets, greater uncertainty about where regional conflicts may erupt, and the risk of the spread of such conflicts make closer military cooperation increasingly important

[1428] The United States must be expected to maintain its global interests and commitments, but these commitments must in the future be fulfilled with far fewer military resources than in the past

[1429] The debate in the United States' about the relationship with Europe may, in the longer term, create uncertainty regarding the extent of the United States' contribution to the defense of Europe and the prioritization of this in relation to other obligations

[1430] This could also have consequences for the military commitment to Norway, including American advance stockpiling, training, and participation in military exercises

[1431] Should we encounter a situation with several regional conflicts at the same time, it is important and necessary for Norway to have close and balanced cooperation with both the United States and the European allies

[1432] Further development and strengthening of mutual reinforcement commitments with European allies can thus give Norway more legs to stand on and thereby contribute to strengthening Norway's strategic policy situation

[1433] Not least, the strategic importance of the petroleum industry requires close cooperation with our most important European allies

[1434] It is further in Norway's interest that the European security and defense identity develops within NATO and with American understanding and acceptance

[1435] The alliance remains dependent on a clear American commitment to European security and defense cooperation

[1436] To the extent that the relationship between the European allies in the EU and the United States weakens, Norway could find itself in a difficult situation

[1437] But NATO's future development will also depend on a number of other factors, such as internal developments in the United States, burden sharing, threat perception, and the willingness and ability of Europeans to participate in military operations outside Europe

[1438] Future cooperation within NATO and Norway's position in this cooperation will not only have political implications, but will also have consequences for the development of the Norwegian defense

[1439] The Government will therefore place great emphasis on ensuring that NATO can continue to solve both traditional and new tasks, and that the organization remains the security policy anchor for all member countries

[1440] Norway's status and role in security policy cooperation were previously strongly influenced by our geostrategic location, and our role in NATO was largely limited to maintaining a strong national invasion defense

[1441] Norway's strategic location remains important, but our ability to influence and contribute has increasingly become a result of our contributions to solving new common security challenges

[1442] This is reflected both in our participation in international peace operations and in our focus on multilateral and bilateral cooperation with partner countries

[1443] Our international network of contacts, status and influence are largely a result of our long tradition of committed international cooperation in NATO and our military involvement in various types of international peace operations

[1444] In other words, Norway's ability and willingness to assume security policy obligations also has positive ripple effects for other parts of our international cooperation

[1445] Security policy instruments

[1446] Most security policy challenges have both political and military aspects

[1447] Therefore, the combination of political and military instruments will often be decisive in meeting these challenges, either nationally or in cooperation with other countries

[1448] pet gives us a unique opportunity to influence international decision-making processes

[1449] The extent to which we succeed depends, among other things, on the resources we deploy, the expertise we have, and the credibility with which we appear in international forums

[1450] Credibility is largely dependent on the ability to maintain our own military apparatus, and thus help ensure continued stability in our immediate areas

[1451] Credibility is also a function of our willingness and ability to assume a reasonable share of the political, economic and military burdens associated with NATO's overall tasks and with international crisis management

[1452] The armed forces are the cornerstone of the government's security policy and must ultimately be able to defend the entire country against military attacks

[1453] However, the national capability for invasion defense is limited to one part of the country at a time

[1454] In addition, the Armed Forces must be able to help handle crises of varying scope and nature, from minor incidents such as border violations or sabotage attacks, to crises involving the use of military force

[1455] Developments in recent years have also increased the need to be able to participate in a broad spectrum of international operations

[1456] It is a key objective that the Armed Forces have the ability to participate in both peacekeeping and peace-building operations together with our allies, our Nordic neighbours, partner countries and other cooperating countries

[1457] In other words, the armed forces must have sufficient capacity

[1458] Parliamentary report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 pacity, flexibility, mobility and readiness to meet a number of different challenges in both war, crisis and peace, both nationally and internationally

[1459] Defence is also a key instrument for developing cooperation and contact with non-allies and thereby contributing to increased trust and stability

[1460] Given the considerable uncertainty associated with a number of security policy issues, it is necessary to maintain an effective and credible intelligence service

[1461] Timely and well-substantiated intelligence is an essential prerequisite for making correct decisions both in peacetime, during incident and crisis management, and as a contribution to strategic warning of attacks on the countryside

[1462] The intelligence service will also be a useful instrument for securing other important national interests, such as environmental monitoring in the surrounding areas

[1463] The security of Norwegian personnel participating in peacekeeping operations is also entirely dependent on sufficient intelligence capacity

[1464] This shows the necessity for Norwegian intelligence personnel to contribute to such operations

[1465] The intelligence service has established cooperation with similar services in other countries

[1466] This has enabled an exchange of information of crucial importance for important national interests, not least through NATO's collective defense

[1467] Challenges in the immediate area The Armed Forces' ability to defend the entire country against military attacks constitutes an important deterrent and stabilizing tool

[1468] The military capability is based on the fact that we receive and can receive allied support, and that we have the ability to cooperate militarily with allied units

[1469] At the same time, the defence must be able to handle more limited military projections, crisis situations and peacetime tasks

[1470] This requires the ability to be mobile and a structure that is sufficiently flexible to be used for a very wide range of tasks

[1471] The various and complex tasks require that further structural development be planned in a holistic manner to a greater extent than previously

[1472] Societal developments are making our own society increasingly vulnerable to sabotage and terrorist attacks

[1473] Large parts of society could be paralyzed if power supplies, telecommunications or other vital infrastructure are disrupted

[1474] Norway can be exposed to such attacks without us being in direct conflict with another state

[1475] To handle such situations in peacetime, the authorities must have a wide range of instruments at their disposal

[1476] The challenges in planning future crisis management will primarily be to organize and prepare the conditions to be able to meet unforeseen, unexpected and complex crises

[1477] This requires a flexible management apparatus that quickly enables the Armed Forces to handle the crisis

[1478] The use of military resources such as the military command apparatus, materiel or personnel in peacetime disasters is therefore an important contribution to the overall national crisis management apparatus

[1479] In peacetime, the Armed Forces must contribute to the assertion of sovereignty on Norwegian territory and to resource management and control at sea

[1480] Norway currently manages a sea area that is seven times larger than mainland Norway

[1481] Active assertion of sovereignty and effective crisis management must be based on military presence and surveillance

[1482] The Armed Forces' tasks related to the protection of petroleum activities, resource management and resource control will probably require increased capacity in the years to come

[1483] The Government will place significant emphasis on active Norwegian participation in multilateral cooperation, especially within NATO

[1484] Our ability to prevent and possibly handle major crises or attacks against Norway will also require political and military support from our allies in the future

[1485] The conditions for receiving such support must be created in peacetime

[1486] This will require a strengthened Norwegian effort in the allied consultation processes

[1487] It will also require increased efforts within military cooperation within NATO through allied exercises and operations, Norwegian participation in the alliance's command and force structure, and by facilitating the reception of allied reinforcements

[1488] Limited allied resources and increased focus on areas other than ours will require a strengthened effort to facilitate conditions for allied exercises and training activities in and around Norway

[1489] The move will also further develop defense-related cooperation with partner countries, including through multilateral project support

[1490] The Government will also place great emphasis on further developing bilateral cooperation with both allies and partner countries

[1491] Both practical military cooperation and bilateral political consultations with our most important current and future allies have great intrinsic value

[1492] In addition, this is a necessary supplement to multilateral cooperation

[1493] Among the partner countries, Sweden, Finland, Russia and the Baltic states will be given particular priority

[1494] This cooperation must be gradually expanded both through political contacts and follow-up practical military cooperation

[1495] Participation in international military operations

[1496] The Armed Forces' participation in international military operations could become an even more important security policy instrument in the years to come

[1497] Our engagement has both a positive direct effect on our overall military capability, and an important indirect effect on our own security, which cannot be seen in isolation from general security policy developments

[1498] International crisis management and planning focused on peace operations

[1499] is today an integrated part of regular defense and force planning in NATO

[1500] Furthermore, international peacekeeping operations will probably be increasingly carried out

[1501] Main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities and development in the period 1999-2002 in cooperation with our Nordic neighbours and other partner countries

[1502] In purely military terms, this concerns our ability to cooperate in multinational and multidimensional operations, not least with regard to strategic mobility and supply support over long distances

[1503] All in all, Norway's ability and willingness to participate in this type of planning and operations will increasingly be considered a measure of our overall security policy credibility

[1504] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities and development in the period 1999-2002 Societal, technological and operational basis

[1505] Defense policy must be part of a comprehensive policy

[1506] This chapter describes other parts of the government's policy that are important for the formulation of defense policy

[1507] This primarily applies to economic policy, industrial policy, regional policy and environmental policy

[1508] But other conditions and developments must also be seen in the context of defense policy

[1509] This applies in particular to the gradual development towards a more vulnerable society, technological developments and the development of new ways of conducting military operations

[1510] Together with the security policy basis from the previous chapter, this forms the basis for the defense policy and development of the Armed Forces, which is described in the next two chapters

[1511] SOCIO-ECONOMIC BASIS

[1512] The government places emphasis on maintaining a healthy economy as a basis for the development of the welfare society

[1513] The long-term foundation for high employment and low unemployment must be laid through an economic policy that contributes to stable economic development

[1514] This requires good and stable framework conditions for Norwegian business

[1515] The Norwegian economy is in the midst of a strong and prolonged economic recovery

[1516] Gross domestic product (GDP) increased in 1996 by over 5 percent and for mainland Norway by just over 3 1/2 percent

[1517] This increase is largely due to growth in petroleum production

[1518] GDP growth is estimated at about 4 percent in 1997, cf. Parliamentary report no

[1519] Norway's large petroleum revenues create opportunities to maintain employment levels and value creation even during periods of economic recession

[1520] At the same time, dependence on a single commodity price makes the Norwegian economy vulnerable

[1521] Projections for macroeconomic developments indicate that growth in total GDP will decline to approximately 2 percent on average for the years 1999-2001, cf. Parliamentary report no

[1522] The Government will use fiscal policy actively to contribute to steady and balanced growth in aggregate public and private demand, and facilitate the implementation of income policy

[1523] In the current economic upswing, fiscal policy must help to curb growth in domestic demand

[1524] In this situation, the government will pursue a tight economic policy

[1525] At the same time, growth projections for the Norwegian economy are uncertain

[1526] For example, a fall in the dollar exchange rate could significantly reduce the profitability of and income from our petroleum production

[1527] The increasing internationalization presents Norwegian businesses with major challenges, but at the same time also provides new opportunities, for example to compete for contracts within the entire EEA area

[1528] To be competitive, companies' ability to adapt and innovate is becoming more important than ever

[1529] The foundation must be laid through interaction with public sector agencies on, among other things, research and development, competence development and infrastructure development

[1530] In addition, an economic policy must be pursued that makes Norwegian producers competitive in terms of costs

[1531] A significant portion of the country's income is currently based on the extraction of oil and gas resources

[1532] The government's net cash flow from petroleum activities is expected to peak just after the turn of the century, at just over 11 percent of GDP, cf. St report no

[1533] It will then gradually fall to just over 6 percent in 2010 and 2 percent in

[1534] Simultaneously with the expected decline in petroleum revenues, the proportion of elderly people in Norway's population will increase

[1535] Social security expenditures will therefore consume an increasing portion of value creation

[1536] about 8 percent of GDP around the turn of the century, and about 15 percent around 2030, cf. St report no

[1537] This "elderly wave" could become the biggest challenge for the Norwegian economy in the coming decades

[1538] In order for the oil wealth to also benefit future generations, and to avoid excessive pressure on the Norwegian economy, the government is emphasizing exploration and licensing policy, and the development of the Government Petroleum Fund

[1539] Economic development and policy constitute an important part of the defense policy foundation

[1540] Although macroeconomic assessments are uncertain, especially in the long term, no strong growth can be expected or planned for on the overall expenditure side of the central government budget

[1541] A responsible and long-term economic policy thus requires prioritization within tight budget limits

[1542] The main lines of defense policy must therefore be drawn up based on a sober, but sufficient, budget level

[1543] INDUSTRY POLICY CONSIDERATIONS

[1544] The ability of the business community to supply the Armed Forces with materiel and other necessary goods and services is of crucial importance to the Armed Forces' operations

[1545] Without such support, the Armed Forces would not be able to carry out its tasks

[1546] As discussed in chapter 4.2, the financial basis for the Armed Forces rests on a healthy socio-economic development in which good development opportunities for the business sector are a central element

[1547] The defense industry constitutes one part of this economic foundation

[1548] It manages expertise, competence and production

[1549] Main guidelines for the Armed Forces' activities and development in the period 1999-2002 capacity that provides ripple effects, innovation and development for the whole of Norwegian society

[1550] Technology developed within the civilian sector is gaining increasing importance

[1551] The use of the same technology for both civilian and military purposes will be important in reducing investment and operating costs for the Armed Forces

[1552] It is therefore important that the Defence's procurement also benefits Norwegian industry and technological development

[1553] In this sense, there is a mutual dependence between the Armed Forces and the business community

[1554] The desire to maintain a national defense industrial capacity also has other reasons, including emergency preparedness

[1555] To ensure resupply from national suppliers if the country were to become isolated, considerable emphasis was previously placed on having a national defense industry of a certain size with emergency stocks of raw materials and semi-finished products

[1556] This still has some validity

[1557] Nevertheless, our preparedness in this area must be assessed somewhat differently today, not least because of the security policy developments and the major industrial structural changes that have taken place

[1558] Norwegian industry is, in a completely different way than before, dependent on partners and subcontractors abroad to produce timely defense equipment

[1559] National expertise and ability to develop and produce technologically high-quality defense equipment represent fundamental insight and experience

[1560] This is important for our long-term defense planning, for being able to act as a well-informed and strong buyer of defense equipment, and for Norway's reputation in general

[1561] Specialized knowledge is also required to operate and maintain modern defense systems

[1562] Without national industrial development and production of defense equipment, such knowledge is rarely available from the civilian side

[1563] National development and production of defense materiel may in many cases be the best solution to meet the Armed Forces' needs and financial framework conditions

[1564] Other countries' equipment is developed to meet needs and levels of ambition that are often fundamentally different from those in Norway

[1565] We need equipment that is adapted to Norwegian geography and climate, and that we can afford to acquire in a certain quantity

[1566] A review of the total costs of a number of Norwegian development projects has shown that the equipment has often been less expensive than similar purchases from abroad

[1567] This applies especially in cases where the equipment would otherwise have to be adapted to Norwegian conditions

[1568] In some areas, the need to protect sensitive technology may also make it impossible or inappropriate to purchase defense equipment from abroad

[1569] For these reasons, the Ministry of Defence places great emphasis on active industrial policy engagement

[1570] This commitment is based on military professional assessments of the Armed Forces' need for modern equipment, which are then seen in the context of other societal interests of a political, economic, technological and industrial nature

[1571] The business policy engagement takes place in close dialogue with the business authorities and industry

[1572] Industrial policy strategy

[1573] The Norwegian defense industry does not have the technological expertise or sufficient production capacity to supply the Armed Forces with all necessary materiel on its own

[1574] Our industry is niche, and technology development within the defense sector occurs as in the civilian sector, in international interaction

[1575] Norway therefore actively participates in international cooperation in the defence equipment sector; bilaterally with selected countries, particularly our allies; and multilaterally within the framework of NATO and the WEU

[1576] The détente in our part of the world has reduced demand for defense equipment and increased competition between suppliers

[1577] At the same time, however, the development costs for new military equipment continue to rise

[1578] This has led to extensive structural rationalization in the defense industry

[1579] Developments have come particularly far in the United States, where the defense industry has been completely restructured in recent years

[1580] In Europe, however, this development has not yet been fully realized

[1581] The European market for defense equipment is more fragmented and limited in size than the American one, and national authorities' desire for control over their own defense industry has prevented extensive rationalization across national borders

[1582] Cross-border cooperation is also complicated by the fact that the equipment must meet multiple and partly different national needs

[1583] Nevertheless, there is a clear tendency towards increasing coordination of material procurement and industrial cooperation in Europe, cf

[1584] in the industrial policy commitment was presented in St prp. no

[1585] Furthermore, the Ministry of Defence presented a strategic plan for research and development in St prp no

[1586] The follow-up to these initiatives was described in Parliamentary Proposal No

[1587] The main goal of the industrial policy strategy is to create conditions for Norwegian industry to obtain the largest possible share of assignments related to the Norwegian Defence's materiel investments

[1588] The strategy will also create conditions for a competitive Norwegian supplier industry

[1589] Traditionally, the question of purchasing Norwegian or foreign equipment has often been considered in connection with the conclusion of the individual contract

[1590] In the case of major acquisitions from abroad, repurchase requirements have also been imposed

[1591] However, both authorities and industry have realized that such an approach is too short-term

[1592] The industrial policy strategy therefore has a time horizon of 10-15 years

[1593] Projects above a certain size are divided into three categories

[1594] One category where conditions seem to be conducive to procurement from Norwegian industry; another category where it seems most appropriate to cooperate with other countries on development and procurement; and a third category where direct purchases from abroad with repurchase requirements seem most appropriate

[1595] The events are facilitated for Norwegian industry through the award of public research and development grants

[1597] The Ministry places great emphasis on the practical follow-up of the industrial policy strategy

[1599] Furthermore, the institute is working on a study of the relationship between military and civilian technology development, and a balance between the use of R&D funds nationally and participation in international development and technology cooperation

[1600] In collaboration with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Defence also aims to develop a unified strategy for further efforts, nationally and internationally

[1601] As part of this work, export regulations must be assessed and further developed on an ongoing basis

[1602] Maintaining foreign companies' willingness to cooperate with Norwegian industry and Norway's credibility as a partner is important in this context

[1604] Buyback and industrial collaboration

[1605] In cases where Norwegian industry does not have the expertise or capacity to meet the Armed Forces' needs, the goal is that Norwegian industry should still be able to contribute to and benefit from the procurements

[1606] This can be done through repurchase from, or other form of industrial collaboration with, the foreign suppliers

[1607] Repurchase is used as a means to maintain and strengthen the Norwegian defense industry's expertise, capacity and market opportunities, as well as to develop cooperation between the Norwegian defense industry and the Armed Forces

[1608] This should preferably take place in areas of direct importance to the Armed Forces

[1609] However, the buyback agreements can also benefit other Norwegian businesses

[1610] Repurchases are mainly divided into the following categories

[1611] development and/or production assignments, establishment of production lines or companies in Norway, establishment of jointly owned industrial companies, investments, transfer of technology, marketing assistance

[1612] In principle, buybacks can have a conservative effect on the structure of markets and the industry

[1613] However, buybacks can also be used actively to accelerate change and long-term cooperation between Norwegian and foreign industry

[1614] In the long term, the defense industry's special status in EU/EEA regulations will probably be reduced and the buyback scheme will be abolished in Europe

[1615] However, the scope and pace of this process are uncertain

[1616] The government will continue to use the instruments that are available to position the Norwegian defense industry so that it is prepared when the buyback regime must be discontinued

[1617] Norway will not take the lead in discontinuing the buy-back scheme as long as other countries maintain this or similar preferential schemes

[1618] To maintain the main features of the settlement pattern and develop viable regions in all parts of the country

[1619] are central goals in government policy

[1620] Developments in recent years have shown that the settlement pattern in a number of peripheral municipalities may be threatened in the long term

[1621] To help stop this development, the government is emphasizing creating a more profitable and growth-oriented business sector in areas with a one-sided business base

[1622] This requires restructuring

[1623] To benefit as much as possible from existing businesses, the transition must be made at an early stage

[1624] Development of new business activities that reduce dependence on individual companies or industries must be based on local resources and strategies

[1625] The government intends that municipalities and county councils will continue to be responsible for designing these strategies

[1626] Despite major reorganizations in recent years, the Armed Forces' nationwide operations will continue to have a major impact on settlement, employment and other activities in a number of municipalities and local communities, particularly in Northern Norway

[1627] There is still a need for significant restructuring of the Armed Forces

[1628] This means new reductions and closures of operations

[1629] Many municipalities and local communities that have traditionally been described as defense-dependent will be affected by these necessary changes

[1630] In some places, businesses will be closed, merged or relocated, while in other places, businesses will be added as part of an overall efficiency plan

[1631] A reduction in the Armed Forces' activities in municipalities that are particularly dependent on defence will, in the short term, lead to fewer jobs directly linked to the Armed Forces and perhaps also reduced demand for goods and services both locally and regionally

[1632] This, in isolation, could lead to reduced employment in other businesses and some relocation in the long term

[1633] The Government will make the restructuring process in the Norwegian Defence as gentle as possible for both Defence personnel and affected municipalities and local communities

[1634] However, a credible Defence Force requires an effective peacekeeping organisation, which is difficult to develop further without, among other things, reducing the Defence Force's traditional commitments in various parts of the country

[1635] Consideration for an efficient organization that can carry out its tasks in a credible manner will therefore be the guiding principle for the organization of the Armed Forces

[1636] However, military presence has value in itself

[1637] The Government will therefore emphasize maintaining a military presence in all parts of the country

[1638] With this as a starting point, and to the extent that it is compatible with the overall security and defense policy goals, the government will seek to limit negative regional political consequences when restructuring the activities

[1639] The government emphasizes creating predictability

[1649] SOCIETY'S VULNERABILITY

[1650] In a democracy, security and effective military defense depend on civil society

[1651] Therefore, changes to activities and structures on the civilian side also constitute an important part of the basis for defense policy

[1652] A worrying development in this context is the gradual, and seemingly incessant, increase in society's vulnerability

[1653] Developments The trend towards a more vulnerable society continues - not necessarily through dramatic changes from one year to the next, but through changes that are significant over time

[1654] Centralization In the last fifty years, there has been a strong population centralization

[1655] This is due in particular to the reduced employment related to agriculture and fishing

[1656] At the same time, a number of societal functions have become more centralized, both within public and private enterprises

[1657] Concentrated and reduced inventories in retail trade are one expression of this

[1658] This form of centralization is primarily due to the pressure for increased economic efficiency and adaptability

[1659] Although greater adaptability can improve the ability to deal with certain types of problems, centralization also creates vulnerable concentrations of people and resources

[1660] Demands for efficiency and adaptation have led to freer markets for services that were previously handled by the public sector

[1661] This makes it in some ways more demanding to secure important societal functions such as telecommunications, power supply and transport

[1662] On the other hand, for example, the abolition of the state monopoly on telecommunications services and the increasing competition for the provision of mobile phone services have made society less vulnerable to disruptions and disruptions in telecommunications

[1663] In addition, the development of local radio, television stations and computer networks has partly made it possible to use other communication channels instead

[1664] Increased use of information technology

[1665] The development and spread of information technology has occurred at a formidable speed

[1666] Today, there is hardly any sector in society that is without electronic information systems

[1667] New technology provides new opportunities, but also creates new challenges

[1668] The use of such technology can simplify and improve most businesses

[1669] Individuals, businesses, countries and regions are being connected more closely through the development of various information networks such as the Internet

[1670] This development erases the meaning of distance and may help slow the tendency towards centralization described earlier

[1671] Increased use of information systems also makes many sectors of society dependent on the functioning of these systems

[1672] It is easy to see that the consequences of a breakdown in financial institutions' computer systems can be significant

[1673] The same applies to computer systems in other important sectors such as energy supply, water supply and telecommunications

[1674] This increasing dependence on electronic information systems creates various forms of vulnerability that can be exploited to create fear, destruction or chaos in society, see also box 4.1. Interdependence Society is also characterized by the fact that important social functions are more closely linked

[1675] This interdependence means that disruptions or breakdowns within one function, such as the electricity supply, can very quickly spread to other functions and systems

[1676] Greater interdependence is also evident across national borders

[1677] On the one hand, dependence on international markets is increasing

[1678] On the other hand, increased international trade and cooperation have made markets more flexible

[1679] Even in a crisis situation, players can emerge who can quickly fill increased demand for specific goods

[1680] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 Non-state actors

[1681] An important development in international politics is the emergence of actors other than nation-states

[1682] Multinational organizations and companies have long been present in the international arena

[1683] But also extremist groups motivated by religious fundamentalism, nationalism or extreme environmental interests, among other things, are spreading their activities across national borders

[1684] Such groups or organizations may resort to violent actions to create pressure or attention for their cause

[1685] Although this development does not increase society's vulnerability, it does increase the risk that someone may exploit this vulnerability

[1686] Information warfare has received considerable attention since the Gulf War

[1687] The United States in particular has taken the lead in exploring the possibilities of this form of warfare

[1688] Information warfare is the attack on and defense of information and associated systems

[1689] In a military sense, such warfare includes attacks of both a physical, psychological and electronic nature

[1690] The increased prevalence and dependence on information technology in military forces also makes it important to protect one's own information and systems

[1691] This defensive side of information warfare seems to be a very big challenge

[1692] Society's increasing dependence on information systems and the trend towards open

[1693] worldwide computer networks have also created vulnerability on the civilian side

[1694] Vulnerable systems can be targeted by both civilian and military actors who wish to create fear, destruction or chaos in society

[1695] As part of a larger attack, such attacks could, for example, disrupt mobilization or impede civilian supply support to military forces

[1696] However, such estimates may also be relevant in connection with terrorist actions or industrial crime

[1697] Global computer networks mean that national borders cannot prevent attacks against our societal functions

[1698] In the worst case, all it takes is knowledge and a computer with a connected modem to spread disinformation or plant computer viruses in systems that are physically located on the other side of the globe

[1699] Information warfare can therefore be carried out without large resources, without warning, without leaving clear traces and without physical destruction, but still with great impact

[1700] Consequences Although these trends point towards both greater and lesser vulnerability in society, society's overall vulnerability is still increasing

[1701] A complex and interdependent society is no stronger than its weakest link

[1702] Without adequate security mechanisms, the critical weaknesses can be exploited by individuals as well as well-organized groups and state actors

[1703] This development becomes particularly worrying when compared with other developments of a technological and military nature, see chapters 4.6 and

[1704] The consequences of a more vulnerable society are therefore discussed in subsequent parts of this chapter and in chapter

[1705] The Government will continue its focus on measures that can reduce society's vulnerability

[1706] This will be a key element in the upcoming long-term plan for civil preparedness

[1707] The long-term plan will be presented to the Storting at approximately the same time as the long-term report for the Armed Forces

[1708] TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT

[1709] Technological developments lead at irregular intervals to profound changes in military forces and operations

[1710] The development of military and civilian technology can create both new threats to Norwegian security and new opportunities for our own defense

[1711] At the same time, the development is characterized by uncertainty about what is politically desirable, technically possible, and what it costs to develop and use such technology

[1712] This multifaceted uncertainty is particularly great in the long term

[1713] The gradual technological improvement of today's weapons systems will continue well into the next century

[1714] Although new operational weapons systems with revolutionary military significance are not expected in the next five to ten years, such weapons systems may see the light of day in the longer term

[1715] Technological development is taking place on a broad front, and there may be reason to point out some of the most important features

[1716] Electronics and Information Technology

[1717] The formidable development in civil electronics and information technology will continue

[1718] On average, capacities double more often than every other year, but the development also leads to smaller size, weight and energy consumption

[1719] This will have great significance for, among other things, military command and information systems, and weapons systems that utilize advanced electronics (see also Box 4.1 on information warfare and Box 9.1 on future operational command and control systems

[1720] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 1997-98 Monitoring

[1721] The development of electronics and information technology makes it possible to develop better sensors and communication systems

[1722] At the same time, such information systems can increasingly be placed on board mobile devices such as aircraft, satellites and other unmanned systems ("drones

[1723] The possibilities for monitoring large land, air and sea areas are therefore gradually improving, but with one important exception

[1724] it will still be difficult to detect activity underwater

[1725] The development of new and significantly more powerful types of explosives will continue

[1726] Greater explosive power can lead to weapons with reduced size or greater effect compared to today's weapons

[1727] Reduced volume and weight will simplify resupply when using such weapons, while greater power will make protection more difficult

[1728] The development of new types of explosives today seems to be moving faster than the development of new protection measures

[1729] Most weapon categories are gaining increasingly longer ranges, higher accuracy and greater effectiveness

[1730] The technology for developing missile systems with high precision and significant range (200-400 km) is known

[1731] Even small countries with limited resources can today develop such systems

[1732] The further development of long-range, unmanned precision weapons could eventually lead to remotely controlled, unmanned tactical aircraft and small drones that will be almost impossible to detect

[1733] Such systems can be used more flexibly than current systems, partly because own personnel are not exposed to risk, and partly because the systems can cost significantly less

[1734] Non-lethal weapons can put personnel or systems out of action for a shorter or longer period of time, but without killing

[1735] Examples of such weapons range from tear gas and rubber bullets, to sophisticated systems based on electronic, acoustic or mechanical means

[1736] Such weapons have not had a prominent place in military arsenals, but experiences from international peace operations, among other things, have increased interest in expanding the means of military forces

[1737] Non-lethal weapons may change both the political framework conditions for the use of military force and the actual use of such force

[1738] They can also help to blur the traditional distinctions between military and other uses of force, and between state and non-state actors

[1739] Laser weapons Laser technology is undergoing rapid development that may eventually have a profound impact on military operations

[1740] In 20 years, there will probably be laser weapons that can shoot down both missiles and aircraft, although we are currently unable to predict the extent and spread of such high-tech capacity

[1741] Laser weapons could become very important, especially in connection with combating missile-based weapons of mass destruction

[1742] Laser weapons could have a major impact on the role of fighter jets

[1743] With allied support of such weapons, the fighter jets will be able to gain significantly greater usefulness

[1744] Above an enemy with such weapons, the fighter jets will be very vulnerable

[1745] Laser weapons can also be developed for use against, for example, helicopters and tanks

[1746] Work has been underway for some time to limit the military use of laser technology in certain types of weapons systems

[1747] The UN Convention of 10 October 1980 on inhumane weapons has now been supplemented by an additional protocol of 13 October 1995 on blinding laser weapons

[1748] The protocol prohibits the use and transfer of laser weapons that are specifically designed to, or have one of their primary combat functions, cause permanent blindness

[1749] Norway has ratified these agreements

[1750] There is reason to highlight some important consequences of technological developments

[1751] Other consequences will be highlighted in subsequent chapters

[1752] Our defense structure and our way of operating must be adapted to technological developments

[1753] Developing systems to exploit or protect against new technology can be both time-consuming and costly

[1754] The requirements for technology and quality must also be balanced against requirements for quantity and flexibility

[1755] A small country like Norway cannot have ambitions to be a technological leader on a broad front, but in order to see opportunities and dangers, knowledge of the multifaceted development of technology is required

[1756] Although the Armed Forces must be prepared to face a technologically modern adversary, Norwegian forces in international peace operations may face actors with a different and in many ways lower technological level

[1757] Such actors can use combinations of military and civilian technology in original ways, they can operate with far lower safety margins than our forces, and they also do not necessarily see themselves as bound by international agreements and conventions

[1758] Over time, the spread of military high technology could also change the framework conditions for such operations

[1759] The level of technology and quality in our national defense must therefore be “good enough” to solve the Defense's tasks, nationally and internationally, in an efficient and credible manner

[1760] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period

[1762] International defence equipment cooperation is described in more detail in chapter

[1763] Technological developments may eventually lead to differences between nations that have and do not have new groundbreaking weapons, such as laser weapons

[1764] However, developing such weapons would be so demanding that only a few countries will have the capability to do so in the foreseeable future

[1766] The United States spends very large resources on research and technological development

[1767] In the long term, this development could result in a clearer American technological hegemony in relation to countries both outside and within NATO

[1768] Such hegemony will manifest itself through a broad spectrum of weapons, command and information systems

[1769] The European allies can either cooperate to develop similar technology or accept dominant American leadership

[1771] Precision-guided weapons have demonstrated the vulnerability of fixed installations

[1772] However, rock structures and heavy concrete structures still provide good protection

[1774] Measures that can protect these parts are important to reduce the vulnerability of existing facilities of this category

[1775] The increased ability to monitor large areas will also make mobile systems more vulnerable

[1776] To protect large and important systems, the systems must be able to operate dispersedly and with frequent changes of position

[1777] At the same time, the importance of electronic countermeasures could increase at the expense of other protective measures

[1779] But creating and maintaining an overview of large ocean areas and long stretches of coastline will require extensive effort

[1780] Greater surveillance capabilities increase the demands on self-defense capabilities for modern surface vessels and drive up costs

[1785] Weapons with ever longer ranges, higher accuracy and greater impact may require new ways of thinking about the traditional areas of responsibility of the defense branches and weapons sectors

[1786] Technological developments therefore not only have consequences for physical weapons and control systems, but must be considered in a broader framework

[1787] MILITARY OPERATIONAL CONCEPTS Future military conflicts may be completely different from past conflicts

[1788] A well-adapted operational concept is a prerequisite for meeting new challenges and applying new technology in the best possible way

[1789] Historical experience has shown that those who do not adapt in line with developments will fall short in a military conflict

[1790] However, the development and implementation of a new operational concept takes many years, and the long-term report is only one step in this process

[1791] A military operational concept describes the basic principles that military forces use in their operations

[1792] The operational concept's fundamental guidelines form the basis for developing techniques at lower levels, operational plans, education and training, force structure and materiel procurement

[1793] Operations, exercises and tests in turn provide the basis for checking and possibly adjusting these solutions

[1794] In this sense, the operational concept permeates all military activities

[1795] During the Cold War, large concentrations of forces faced each other on both sides of the Iron Curtain

[1796] On the western side, there was fear of a massive attack across a broad front in Europe

[1797] The goal was to hold the front line until overseas reinforcements could create a military solution

[1798] In military terminology, this is called attrition-oriented warfare

[1799] Theoretically, the party with the greatest resources would ultimately win

[1800] After the Cold War, NATO developed a new strategy with an emphasis on crisis management and war prevention operations

[1801] The forces became smaller, but at the same time more mobile and flexible in order to be able to quickly concentrate for regional efforts

[1802] This accelerated the conceptual development towards more indirect and maneuver-oriented operational patterns

[1803] This development has also influenced Norwegian defense planning, and in June 1995 the Chief of Defense presented his new operational concept

[1804] The new Norwegian operational concept

[1805] All states or military organizations have weaknesses that are crucial to the ability or willingness to use military force

[1806] Such critical points will not necessarily be the opponent's military combat units, but could just as easily be his command apparatus, infrastructure

[1807] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 structure, supply lines or other critical resources

[1808] Since the critical points can vary from actor to actor and from situation to situation, it can be a major challenge to identify these points in a counterparty in a given situation

[1809] The second main question is how to target them

[1810] Maneuver warfare places the emphasis on hitting an opponent's critical points through rapid and unexpected maneuvers that put him in such a difficult situation that he chooses to abandon further combat - even though his combat units may be more or less intact in isolation

[1811] The enemy is therefore not met massively and on a broad front, but through attacks against selected, and for him, critically important points

[1812] In this way, even a numerically inferior force can make an opponent give up his military goals without necessarily defeating him physically

[1813] Maneuver warfare can also help reduce one's own losses because one seeks to avoid the opponent's strongest units as much as possible

[1814] The Norwegian operational concept is based on the principles of maneuver warfare

[1815] Nevertheless, it is important to maintain sufficient ability to meet an opponent's main force with its own combat units in order to be able to advantageously utilize the land or waters in our particular geography

[1816] Our operational concept therefore emphasizes a balanced ability to carry out operations of different nature

[1817] In international peace operations, Western countries have so far been able to rely on military superiority over local actors

[1818] Such imbalances in power mean that local actors often seek to compensate for this in other ways, for example through terrorist actions directed against the intervention forces' home countries or against broader parts of the international community

[1819] Technological developments in combination with the increasing vulnerability of Western societies may contribute to making such "asymmetric" threats more relevant in the future

[1820] An adversary who is capable of utilizing modern technology in effective ways, for example to paralyze important national or international computer networks, will not necessarily be pacified by a military defeat

[1821] Nor are there necessarily suitable military countermeasures against such threats, cf. chapter

[1822] The transition to a maneuver-oriented operational concept has consequences for all military activities

[1823] Some of the consequences are discussed below, while others are highlighted in subsequent chapters

[1824] Requirements for the Armed Forces' activities

[1825] In order to identify and hit critical points on an opponent, good intelligence, weapons systems and forces with varied capabilities, and the ability to coordinate efforts are required, among other things

[1826] But maneuver warfare is also based on the ability to wage war at a high pace and with high intensity

[1827] Initiative and speed are required at all levels, mobile and flexible forces, and personnel with high competence and training standards at all levels

[1828] This illustrates how guiding the operational concept is for the entire Armed Forces' activities

[1832] This makes it necessary to further develop today's training and practice patterns

[1950] INTRODUCTION Defence policy guidelines

[1951] Norwegian defense policy must take into account challenges of varying nature in the years ahead

[1952] Although the danger of a large-scale military attack on Western Europe has been eliminated, and Norway today does not face any military threat, the danger of smaller, armed conflicts has by no means disappeared from our continent

[1953] We have no guarantee that such conflicts will not spread - not even to our own area

[1954] Norway therefore still faces potential military challenges in the high north

[1955] In the foreseeable future, the significant military capabilities located in our immediate vicinity will constitute an important premise for defense policy

[1956] The trend towards more vulnerable societies, and the development of weapons with ever longer ranges, higher accuracy and greater impact, also raises military challenges other than conventional war

[1957] Through limited and selective use of armed force, sabotage or terrorist attacks, key societal functions can be paralyzed

[1958] Norway can be exposed to such attacks without us being in direct conflict with another state

[1959] At the same time, we are facing other challenges

[1960] Norway manages a sea area that is seven times larger than mainland Norway, and we are one of the world's most significant oil and gas exporters

[1961] Active assertion of sovereignty, effective resource control and management of many types of crises must be based on the use of military resources

[1962] Therefore, this type of challenge also constitutes an important part of defense policy

[1963] Norway will continue to depend on NATO cooperation to be able to handle major crises and military attacks, and our defense policy will continue to be based on and support membership in the alliance

[1964] However, Norwegian defense policy must take into account the profound changes in and around NATO, which, among other things, means that Norway receives less attention from our allies than before

[1965] The challenges of defense policy are many: weighing the probabilities and consequences of different types of challenges, weighing near-term challenges against potential longer-term challenges, and on this basis laying the foundations for a credible Defense

[1966] But defense policy is not just about being able to meet negative developments

[1967] Defence policy should also promote positive development

[1968] A credible for

[1969] This answer helps to ensure continued stability in our immediate areas, and represents the basis for participation in broad international cooperation to create increased trust and stability, and to resolve international conflicts and prevent new ones from arising

[1970] Defence policy constitutes the central part of the government's security policy

[1971] The changes in our strategic situation and the considerable uncertainty about further security policy developments will require a broader alignment of defence policy and the Armed Forces than previously

[1972] This means that the importance of defense policy and the Defense has changed, but not necessarily reduced

[1973] This chapter describes the main lines of the government's defense policy

[1974] First, the defense policy goals are described

[1975] The fundamental pillars of our defence concept are then assessed

[1976] a national balanced defense, allied military cooperation and international cooperation, total defense and conscription, based on the changes that have occurred and are expected to occur around us

[1977] Together, this forms the basis for formulating which tasks the Defence must solve to contribute to fulfilling the goals of Norwegian security and defence policy

[1978] Defence policy goals

[1979] Based on the overall security policy goals described in chapter 3.1, the defense policy goals indicate how the Armed Forces can contribute to our security

[1980] The goals of Norwegian defence policy are the following: military presence and visibility; ability to provide and exchange risk assessments and early warnings; ability to handle incidents and crises; ability to defend Norwegian land, sea and air territory against military attacks; ability to cooperate militarily with allies and participate in international force structures and operations; defence-related cooperation with other countries and within international organisations. Sufficient military presence and visibility are necessary to assert Norwegian sovereignty in peacetime

[1981] Visibility also contributes to raising awareness about total defense and conscription in our own society

[1982] A well-developed intelligence and surveillance service that can provide reliable risk assessments and early warnings is a prerequisite for preventing and handling incidents, crises and military attacks

[1983] A credible defense is our most important tool for continued peace and stability

[1984] The armed forces must therefore be organized, equipped and trained to be able to participate in the authorities' handling of incidents and crises, and if necessary, defend the country against military attacks

[1985] The ability to cooperate militarily with allied forces on Norwegian territory is an integral part of our ability to handle crises and military attacks

[1986] At the same time, Norwegian military forces must be able to participate in 1997-98 St report no

[1987] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 international operations outside Norwegian territory, also outside NATO's area of ​​responsibility

[1988] In order to contribute to stability and peaceful development, emphasis must also be placed on other forms of defense-related cooperation with other countries and within international organizations

[1989] In this context, this particularly includes cooperation with our partner countries, both bilaterally and within the PfP framework in NATO, and cooperation on solving military tasks within the UN and the OSCE

[1990] Norwegian defense policy is based on four mutually reinforcing principles: a balanced national defense, allied military cooperation and international cooperation, total defense, conscription

[1991] Together, these principles can be called our defense concept, that is, our fundamental idea about the orientation of Norwegian defense policy

[1992] This concept forms the main framework for our military defense development and operations

[1993] Based on the changes in our surroundings, the government sees a continuing need to further develop defense policy within these frameworks

[1994] In the current situation, the government believes it is inappropriate to consider alternative defense concepts

[1995] A national balanced defense

[1996] An effective and credible defense cannot be built up in a few years

[1997] For example, it takes ten to fifteen years to acquire new generations of frigates and fighter jets, and build up expertise to utilize such advanced systems

[1998] The equipment acquisitions and competence building in the coming four years will consequently constitute main components of the Defence we will have in ten to fifteen years

[1999] Therefore, defense policy and defense planning must be oriented towards the long term, and in the long term, the possibility of new military threats to Norwegian territory cannot be ruled out

[2000] The potential military threats in the long term also include the danger of a military attack with the aim of occupying large parts of Norwegian territory

[2001] Such an invasion would require large land, air and naval forces

[2002] The expected development of military capacity in our immediate area does not indicate any potential danger of an invasion of the entire country, even in the long term

[2003] Therefore, an invasion would hardly be able to encompass more than one part of the country, but such an invasion could very well be supported by limited actions and attacks against the rest of the country

[2004] The government's ambition therefore continues to be to maintain the ability for time-limited invasion defense in one part of the country at a time

[2005] A credible invasion defense of Norway over time requires resources far beyond what can be allocated from the Norwegian defence budget

[2006] Our national invasion defense is therefore inextricably linked to the other pillars of the Norwegian defense concept

[2007] Support from our allies will be crucial to being able to solve such a comprehensive security challenge as invasion defense over time

[2008] Our geographical location on the outskirts of Europe and the need for military reinforcements on a significant scale also make it necessary to maintain an independent national invasion defense with a certain amount of endurance

[2009] A surprise military attack must not cause the Armed Forces to collapse immediately pending sufficient allied reinforcement support

[2010] A balanced Norwegian defense makes it possible to bear the brunt of the defense effort in the initial phase of a war and makes cooperation with and management of allied reinforcements on Norwegian territory more credible

[2011] The ability to defend against invasion in one part of the country does not mean that the rest of the country can be left open

[2012] A balanced defense must have the ability to monitor and defend the entire country against limited attacks, sabotage or terrorist attacks, regardless of whether these challenges are related to an attempted invasion or not

[2013] A balanced defense also includes the ability for military presence, intelligence, and incident and crisis management

[2014] The Armed Forces must therefore have sufficient capability to solve a number of different tasks and meet various challenges in peace, crisis and war

[2015] Although the probability of military attacks seems small, the consequences could be catastrophic if we do not have a certain ability to meet such challenges

[2016] The continuation of a national balanced defense that has a time-limited ability to meet a major military attack against one part of the country, the ability to meet limited attacks or threats throughout the country, and the ability to fulfill other important tasks is therefore, in the government's view, the only responsible and realistic alternative

[2017] Nevertheless, it is both right and necessary to adapt our nationally balanced defense to the changes in our environment

[2173] DEFENCE TASKS

[2174] Based on the defense policy goals and the defense concept, the tasks of the Armed Forces can be divided into nine main groups

[2175] invasion defense, territorial defense, crisis management, assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority, intelligence service, security service, international military engagement, rescue service and other socially beneficial use of the Armed Forces

[2176] Invasion defense is the Armed Forces' most demanding task and governs the main lines of the Armed Forces' structure and activities

[2177] The ambition for national invasion defense to meet a major military attack is limited to one part of the country at a time

[2178] Militarily, Northern Norway is still the potentially most vulnerable part of the country, and large parts of our invasion defense will continue to be deployed in this part of the country

[2179] However, to safeguard the need for strategic freedom of action, the capability for invasion defense must, if necessary and over time, be able to be shifted to another part of the country

[2180] The ability to defend against invasion cannot be seen in isolation from our alliance affiliation

[2181] Allied reinforcements will be crucial to resisting a comprehensive attack on Norway

[2182] However, in light of our geographical location, we must be able to face an attack on our own in the first phase

[2183] This requires a national ability to perform the most vital functions in invasion defense

[2184] The defense of one part of the country will depend on supplies and reinforcements from other parts of the country

[2185] For example, the ability to secure the sea transport lines between Central and Northern Norway, as well as the management apparatus and critically important societal functions in Southern Norway, will be of crucial importance in order to be able to conduct extensive military operations in the north

[2186] An effective and sustained invasion defense in one part of the country cannot therefore be seen in isolation from the defense of the rest of the country

[2187] Based on the current security policy situation, the warning period for a possible invasion of Norwegian territory is long

[2188] However, a limited attack that could initiate an invasion in the north would have a shorter warning time

[2189] Our ordinary operations must be adapted to the length of the preparation time

[2190] Based on the current situation, sufficient invasion defense capacity must be built up within three months

[2191] However, the notice period may change over time

[2192] The capacity must be made so robust that it provides the ability to exercise effective invasion defense over a certain period of time

[2193] Territorial defense The Armed Forces shall maintain a military presence in all parts of the country

[2194] This presence must still be of such a magnitude in 1997-98 that a potential attacker must carry out a visible force buildup before offensive operations can be launched

[2195] This will give Norwegian authorities time to consult our allies and make necessary decisions about raising the state of readiness, mobilizing and transferring forces

[2196] In addition, the territorial defense will contribute to territorial surveillance and secure the management apparatus and important infrastructure against sabotage and limited attacks

[2197] For limited attacks, the warning time can be very short

[2198] Territorial defense is mainly handled by departments from the Home Guard and the Army

[2199] The Home Guard will play a particularly important role through its local affiliation, decentralized organization and extensive cooperation with civil society

[2200] The Territorial Defence must ensure that the rest of the Defence can mobilise and that the management apparatus is able to make independent decisions

[2201] Likewise, these forces must ensure that important societal functions are maintained

[2202] The forces must be organized and equipped so that these tasks can be carried out over time

[2203] The ordinary operability of parts of the territorial defence forces must therefore be at a higher level than that of the forces in the invasion defence

[2205] Coordinated actions will be needed to eliminate the crisis, prevent unwanted escalation or limit military confrontations

[2207] The use of instruments must be appropriate to the purpose

[2209] The Armed Forces must therefore be able to help handle crises of varying scope and nature

[2211] Effective crisis management therefore requires the ability to quickly deploy units and departments from the Armed Forces, and the ability to reinforce these, if necessarily also with units and departments from our allies

[2221] Assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority

[2222] The government places great emphasis on effective assertion of sovereignty over Norwegian territory, including territorial waters, as well as the exercise of authority and resource control in Norway's large maritime areas

[2223] Asserting sovereignty requires the ability to handle both minor and major incidents at sea, in the air and on land

[2224] The Armed Forces must therefore be able to quickly and effectively repel any violations of Norwegian territory in peacetime, and be able to isolate a conflict by quickly concentrating appropriate military capacity in the areas where a violation occurs

[2225] In peacetime, asserting sovereignty at sea means checking that those traveling in our territorial waters have permission to do so

[2226] In times of serious crisis and war, enforcing Norwegian sovereignty involves the ability to prevent an adversary or other foreign vessels from accessing Norwegian territorial waters

[2227] The ability to control must therefore be maintained and further developed

[2228] The Armed Forces must ensure sufficient information about and control of foreign vessels' movements in Norwegian territorial waters

[2229] An important tool is the port of call regulations, which regulate the passage of both military and non-military vessels in our waters

[2230] Since the submission of the previous long-term report, these regulations have been simplified and adapted to the current situation

[2231] Great emphasis is placed on effective control and fair enforcement to ensure respect for the port regulations

[2232] Regular presence in Norwegian areas of interest and control of maritime resource management contribute to safeguarding Norwegian rights at sea

[2233] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall monitor and maintain control of activity in all waters under Norwegian jurisdiction

[2234] In connection with international agreements, the Armed Forces shall ensure a regular presence in adjacent international waters of importance to Norwegian interests, see box

[2235] The exercise of authority at sea involves control and supervision of large ocean areas in fields such as fisheries management, resource extraction, environmental protection and maritime traffic

[2236] The exercise of authority requires that the Armed Forces monitor and control activity in all waters, see box

[2237] In peacetime, resource management and resource control at sea are an important task for the Armed Forces

[2238] In this context, the Coast Guard plays a key role

[2239] The Armed Forces also carry out surveillance, assert sovereignty and exercise authority in Norwegian airspace

[2240] The ability to continuously monitor Norwegian airspace and adjacent areas must be maintained

[2241] The border guard service on land is an important part of the Armed Forces' ability to assert sovereignty and must at all times have the capacity to effectively carry out its tasks

[2242] Active assertion of sovereignty and effective crisis management require military surveillance of and presence in Norwegian territory

[2243] Norwegian geography places high demands on these functions

[2244] The Armed Forces must therefore identify and assess the opportunities inherent in new technology and improved mobility to ensure sufficient surveillance and presence capabilities

[2245] In times of crisis and war where emergency legislation has come into effect, securing petroleum installations is a military task

[2246] In such a situation, allied support can also be expected

[2247] Even in peacetime, the Armed Forces will perform important functions in connection with the security and protection of offshore petroleum installations because it is primarily the Armed Forces that has the capacity and expertise to operate on the shelf

[2248] A main function will be to carry out preventive measures in the form of notification, monitoring, presence and control

[2249] The Armed Forces must also be able to increase preparedness and presence in the event of a possible attack, and to carry out operations in response to an attack

[2250] This requires the ability to coordinate efforts from all branches of defense and the ability to operate together with allied forces

[2251] The forces whose main task is to assert sovereignty must carry out this activity as part of their normal operations

[2252] Other forces that are to support the assertion of sovereignty in connection with handling incidents must have ordinary operational capabilities that are adapted to the length of the preparation period
