[2257] The Coast Guard The Coast Guard vessels, as part of the Navy, have as their main task in peacetime to contribute to asserting Norwegian sovereignty on Norwegian territory, including territorial waters and Norwegian sovereign rights in maritime areas under Norwegian jurisdiction

[2258] Asserting Norwegian sovereignty and Norwegian sovereign rights in maritime areas under Norwegian jurisdiction involves, among other things, supervision, inspection and control in Norway's economic zone, the fisheries protection zone around Svalbard, in the fisheries zone at Jan Mayen and on the Norwegian continental shelf

[2259] Norway also has a management responsibility for fishery resources in international waters within the framework of international law

[2260] However, regarding enforcement, this can only happen pursuant to international agreement

[2261] Through the internal coast guard, which was established in 1995, the Coast Guard also assists other government agencies that have tasks in coastal areas

[2262] Examples of such assistance are rescue preparedness, oil spill preparedness and assistance with customs supervision

[2263] The Coast Guard's tasks in times of emergency and war are protection of transport lines along the coast, guard and warning tasks, and maritime surveillance

[2264] The Coast Guard Act of 13 June 1997 provides comprehensive regulation of the Coast Guard's organization, responsibilities and authority

[2265] The Act also provides a legal basis for the Coast Guard's exercise of authority

[2266] The Coast Guard's ability to carry out its tasks is largely linked to the presence of suitable units and competent personnel

[2271] The Air Force contributes to the Coast Guard's operations through a squadron of maritime aircraft with surveillance and patrol capacity

[2272] To support the Coast Guard's tasks, emphasis will also be placed on utilizing the Armed Forces' other resources, not least resources for surveillance and operational management

[2285] Security service The Minister of Defence has the overall and constitutional responsibility for the preventive general security service throughout the state administration, cf. Royal Decree of 24 September

[2286] The Ministry of Defence is thus responsible for regulatory and supervisory responsibilities in this area

[2305] International military involvement

[2306] International engagement has become an increasingly important task for the Armed Forces

[2307] It includes not only military cooperation within NATO and participation in international peace operations, but also other forms of defense-related cooperation, both bilaterally and within multilateral organizations

[2308] However, the bulk of our international military engagement takes place through participation in multinational force structures and international peace operations

[2309] The Armed Forces must be able to quickly and cost-effectively make suitable contributions to a variety of types of operations

[2310] It is therefore important that relevant units for international efforts are identified and prepared in advance to the greatest extent possible

[2311] This is a challenge, especially for armies, because it is resource-intensive to have larger standing departments on standby for international operations

[2312] Current naval and air forces are mainly static and can more easily adjust their organization for different missions abroad

[2370] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period

[2371] The structure and activities of the Armed Forces The development of the Armed Forces must be adapted to the ongoing and long-term changes in our environment and our society

[2372] Most NATO countries are constantly reducing the size of their military forces and are increasingly aligning their defense planning with the ability to participate with emergency forces in international operations outside the territories of NATO countries

[2373] Although there are significant individual differences, the alliance's member countries have spent a steadily decreasing share of their society's value creation on military purposes throughout the first half of the 1990s

[2374] However, developments in the last couple of years may indicate that these reductions are leveling off

[2375] Norway's military spending, measured as a share of our gross domestic product, is now at the average level for the European NATO countries, and somewhat below the average for the alliance as a whole

[2376] The United States is not planning dramatic changes in its force structure and preparedness, but the development of American defense in the longer term is still uncertain

[2377] At the same time, the United States invests far more in research and development than the other NATO countries

[2378] This could ultimately have consequences for both political, material and military cooperation within NATO

[2379] The conventional military capabilities in our immediate area also constitute an important premise for defense planning

[2380] The Russian armed forces have major restructuring problems

[2381] In the Leningrad Military District, there has been a significant reduction in military capacity and operability in recent years

[2382] The conventional forces are nevertheless better equipped than in most other regions

[2383] The Russian Northern Fleet's main task today is related to strategic nuclear weapons, and the fleet has limited capacity to perform other tasks in addition

[2384] Sweden's defense has been greatly reduced so far in the 1990s

[2385] Further reductions in the Swedish Armed Forces are planned in the coming years, and large parts of the force structure are based on the assumption of a long warning period

[2386] Finland has not reduced its military structure and readiness to the same extent as Sweden

[2387] The transition to a maneuver-oriented operational concept also has an important impact on the structure and activities of the Armed Forces

[2388] Such a way of operating requires the ability to conduct coordinated combat at high speed and with high intensity

[2389] Mobile and flexible forces are required, and personnel with high competence and training standards at all levels

[2390] Maneuver-oriented operations must be seen in the context of technological development, and our new operational concept sets clear minimum requirements for what level of technology and quality is good enough for the Armed Forces

[2391] At the same time, the demands for technology, flexibility and quality in our forces must be balanced against the need to have a sufficient range of forces to ensure a certain level of endurance and, if necessary, to be able to defend different parts of the country simultaneously

[2392] The ability and willingness to change characterize the development of an effective and modern defense

[2393] At the same time, defense planning requires a long-term perspective and the activities of the Armed Forces require a minimum of stability

[2394] Recruitment, competence building and investments over the next four years will constitute key elements of the Norwegian Armed Forces for decades to come

[2395] This chapter describes goals and guidelines for the future structure and activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces

[2396] These goals and guidelines form the basis for following up on the main political guidelines described in the report

[2397] Relationships between the tasks, structure and activities of the Armed Forces

[2398] The tasks of the Armed Forces are the starting point for the development of the Armed Forces' structure and the orientation of the Armed Forces' activities

[2399] Ensuring a balanced and flexible ability to solve the full range of tasks - invasion defense, territorial defense, crisis management, assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority, intelligence service, security service, international military engagement, rescue service and other socially beneficial use of the Defense - constitutes the very core of defense planning

[2400] There are many and sometimes complicated connections between the tasks, structure and activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces

[2401] The various units and sectors of the Armed Forces contribute to solving different tasks and different parts of the same task

[2402] The tasks of the Armed Forces can be divided into two main categories, see Figure 6.1: peacetime tasks that the Armed Forces perform as part of their ordinary activities in peacetime, i.e. assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority, intelligence services, security services, international military engagement, rescue services and other socially beneficial uses of the Armed Forces

[2403] war tasks that the Armed Forces carry out in crisis and war based on mobilization measures

[2404] War tasks have the greatest significance for the structure and activities of the Armed Forces, but are only carried out after mobilization

[2405] Crises can encompass a number of different situations, and the task of crisis management therefore falls under both main categories

[2406] The ability to solve the Armed Forces' tasks in peace, crisis and war must be based on the Armed Forces' force structure, control

[2407] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 the response capability of the forces and their endurance

[2408] The spectrum of tasks, with invasion defense as the most demanding, sets the requirements

[2409] Most of the Armed Forces' capabilities are the result of competence building and investments over the past decades, but these capabilities naturally age from one year to the next

[2410] The development and maintenance of the force structure therefore forms the basis for the Armed Forces' activities in peacetime

[2411] At the same time, the Norwegian Armed Forces' peace organization must solve the peacetime tasks

[2412] Different parts of the Armed Forces' activities must be carefully coordinated with each other

[2413] The use of personnel, materiel, property, buildings and facilities is managed through operational areas to create a force structure, which in turn makes it possible to solve the Armed Forces' tasks

[2414] The plans are thus implemented by making the necessary resources available for the Armed Forces' activities through the annual budgets

[2415] Continued restructuring

[2416] A war-preventive defense requires a credible ability to solve the Armed Forces' tasks at all times

[2417] This can only be achieved by utilizing all resources made available to the Armed Forces in peace, crisis and war as effectively as possible

[2418] The previous long-term report initiated a comprehensive restructuring process to develop a better balanced defence

[2419] Profound changes have been made to the Norwegian Armed Forces' force structure and peacekeeping organization

[2420] Several of the measures that will help secure necessary investments through operational savings are still being implemented

[2421] It will still be some time before the effects become apparent

[2422] At the same time, weaknesses have been uncovered in the restructuring process, including those related to the extraordinary personnel situation in parts of the business in

[2423] In order to implement the transition, it has also been necessary to temporarily downgrade certain areas, including education, training and practice

[2424] With the structure and activities that this announcement proposes, there is hardly any room for transfers from operations to investments in the coming years

[2425] The continued restructuring must, above all, make it possible to strengthen critically important activities on the operational side without damaging investments

[2426] However, a defense in transition does not mean rationalization in the narrow sense

[2427] Equally important is ensuring the Defence's ability to meet the challenges that the future can and will bring

[2477] A credible defense must therefore be geared towards long-term and partly unpredictable challenges

[2478] In light of the uncertainty about security policy developments, the government will continue a national balanced defense in order to defend the entire country

[2479] The ability to repel an invasion attempt will, however, be limited to one part of the country at a time and will over time be dependent on allied support

[2480] However, meeting other and more limited forms of attack, such as a comprehensive missile attack, may also require such large resources that allied support is necessary

[2481] The risk of a major military attack on Norway is considered very small in the coming years

[2497] Main guidelines The tasks in peace, crisis and war must be seen in context

[2498] The future force structure and organization of the Armed Forces must therefore be suitable for handling this entire range of tasks in a cost-effective manner

[2499] A comprehensive defense means that the different parts of the force structure are carefully coordinated with each other and with the different parts of the Armed Forces' activities

[2500] Such a whole will not only contribute to the efficient use of resources, but also provide freedom of action to expand our military defense if necessary

[2501] Freedom of action Defense planning requires a long-term perspective, but long-term goals are fraught with great uncertainty

[2502] With the uncertainty about future challenges, it is important to be prepared for the possibility of changes in the governing assumptions regarding the composition, dimensioning and initial disposition of the forces

[2503] The long-term plans for the development of the force structure must therefore provide freedom of action and, as far as possible, be based on structural elements that will be important to possess regardless of the orientation of the Armed Forces

[2504] This means, among other things, that the force structure must not be made critically dependent on stationary infrastructure in order to operate

[2505] As a result of the long-term nature of material procurement and the development of the organization, the target structure for 2006 is to a significant extent determined by investments that have already been decided to be made or are being implemented

[2506] This is of course even more true in the period

[2507] It is important that the investment decisions made in the coming years do not unnecessarily restrict freedom of action in the longer term

[2508] The armed forces' force structure must be modernized and maintained continuously

[2509] The best possible ratio between the quality and quantity of the forces is decisive for the performance of the structure

[2510] A modern combat environment and operational concept place demands on quality

[2511] The aim for the quality level of the forces is a soberly assessed minimum level, not high-tech defense

[2512] At the same time, a necessary scale of forces must be maintained to ensure a certain level of endurance and ability to defend several parts of the country simultaneously

[2513] This applies not least to the Army

[2514] For the Air Force and Navy, there will be a somewhat greater focus on new technology at the expense of the 1997-98 number of units

[2515] However, the development of military capabilities, military operations and military technology indicates that the minimum requirements for the quality and scope of forces are neither unambiguous nor unchangeable over time

[2516] Joint operations The Armed Forces' overall operational capability is critically dependent on forces from different parts of the organization being able to support and reinforce each other

[2517] A force structure that accommodates a broad spectrum of capabilities provides better opportunities for organizing forces according to task

[2518] This means, among other things, that the overall structure of the Armed Forces should make it possible to organize combat units in a flexible manner

[2519] Many smaller units must be able to be coordinated for effective efforts

[2520] Larger units must be able to separate independent combat units to solve limited missions

[2521] Joint operations require the ability to collaborate between the branches of defense, including joint solutions for command, control, communication and information

[2538] The ambitions of a time-limited defense against invasion in one part of the country, securing allied reinforcement operations and securing against limited attacks throughout the country guide the design of the Army

[2539] Divisions with divisional troops and three divisional brigades will constitute the Army's main contribution to the invasion defense

[2540] In order to reinforce invasion defense, as well as for territorial defense, crisis management and assertion of sovereignty, the Army will have three independent brigades and approximately 20 independent battalion units

[2541] Furthermore, the district commands will have units to support the division, the independent brigades and the territorial forces

[2542] In addition to the purely national tasks, our capabilities for international efforts on the army side will be organized within one of the independent brigades

[2543] Although the Army's force structure is largely in place organizationally, it will take time to provide the departments with the necessary materiel

[2544] The army will have a great need to reacquire major equipment as it becomes obsolete

[2545] Any acquisition of tanks and artillery will be particularly demanding

[2546] Shortages or obsolescence of key materiel must be accepted if the scope of the force structure is to be maintained

[2547] Until 2006, the division and one independent brigade will be prioritized

[2548] This means that during this period only marginal investments are being made in two of the Army's six brigades

[2549] Other departments will receive some new equipment, and used equipment to the extent that such material can be transferred from higher priority departments that are receiving new equipment

[2550] Around 2006, the quality of the lowest priority units in the Army may become so marginal that consideration must be given to reducing the number and restructuring parts of the territorial forces

[2551] Although some units have gained greater mobility, the restructuring of the Army has reduced the ability for nationwide territorial defense

[2782] Education and training

[2783] Education and training of commanders

[2784] The future combat environment, new military operational concepts, utilization of increasingly advanced technology, the requirement for efficient management and restructuring place high demands on competence in the Armed Forces

[2785] A modern and dynamic defence therefore places high quality demands on training, continuing education and further education

[2786] Lifelong learning is becoming increasingly important, and the Armed Forces must be at the forefront of developments in this field

[2787] The Norwegian Armed Forces' international involvement is extensive

[2788] This also presents challenges to the Armed Forces' educational institutions

[2789] Military training will continue to be the core element of education, but must also be seen in a broader perspective that also emphasizes the ability to cooperate with forces from other nations, understanding of ethnic, cultural and religious differences, integrity and humanity

[2790] A central competency requirement for military personnel in general, and officers in particular, is knowledge of the basic rules of international humanitarian law

[2791] Such knowledge is particularly important for personnel who will participate in international operations

[2792] The Armed Forces' military educational institutions must maintain a high level of quality

[2793] The new officer regulation provides for a more flexible education system in which the officer's prior learning will be a greater determinant of further advancement

[2794] Alternative career paths should help meet both the needs of the Armed Forces and the individual's desire for career choices

[2795] In light of the strategic plan for competence development, the possibilities for further coordination of the Armed Forces' educational institutions will be examined in more detail

[2796] Where conditions are right, civilian college and university environments should form the basis for competence building rather than building up separate competence environments in the Armed Forces

[2858] Investments In order to maintain and develop the Armed Forces' force structure in line with the guidelines in chapter 6.3, significant investments in materiel, property, buildings and facilities are required over the coming years

[2859] The government emphasizes that this necessary modernization is carried out in a sober and responsible manner

[2860] The materiel investments will contribute to a balanced and cost-effective development of the Armed Forces' force structure and operational capabilities

[2861] In the period 1999-2002, investments in equipment of approximately NOK 24 billion are planned

[2862] Operational conditions, as well as considerations of effective peacekeeping, indicate that the Armed Forces must be viewed as a whole

[2863] A comprehensive assessment based on the Armed Forces' tasks and functions is an important prerequisite for making sound investment decisions

[2864] All investments must therefore be assessed in relation to the current material balance and in light of realistic estimates for future investment frameworks

[2865] To ensure a balanced material stock and the necessary freedom of action in structural development, two main considerations must be taken into account when making investment decisions

[2866] Firstly, investment must

[2867] The resources are directed towards those parts of the force structure where the needs are greatest

[2868] High-priority equipment should therefore be acquired before equipment that is less essential to the Armed Forces' operations

[2869] Secondly, material procurement must be in accordance with sober assessments of operational needs

[2870] The Norwegian Armed Forces' project management system must be further developed with an emphasis on simplifying decision-making processes

[2871] The Norwegian Armed Forces' investment projects are usually long-term in nature and can extend over 10-15 years

[2872] It is therefore difficult to estimate the total costs correctly

[2873] Increased focus on life cycle costs and logistics processes will further contribute to greater precision in long-term plans

[2874] Routines must be introduced that make it more possible to correct/terminate projects if governing assumptions, such as economics and security policy, change significantly during the duration of the project

[2875] Budget overruns, delays and inadequate deliveries in individual projects will affect the Armed Forces' ability to carry out other material investments in accordance with plans and operational needs

[2876] Methods must therefore be developed to improve control of critical factors and uncertainties, both in the individual project and in the overall project portfolio

[2877] This will help to further develop a balanced force structure over time

[2878] Traditional procurement methods, with their emphasis on large series and low unit prices, have proven to create long-term commitments that reduce the freedom to make updates, adjustments and adaptations to the force structure

[2879] This calls for more flexible procedures

[2880] In future procurements, the following alternatives must be considered: use of options to reduce the impact of uncertainty and ensure that marginal units are not acquired; use of options must be considered against the additional cost this may entail purchasing smaller series to achieve greater flexibility; this requires, among other things, an overall assessment of any increased investment costs over time and increased costs of continued operation of old equipment; purchase of used equipment to contribute to low unit costs; assessments of such purchases must place particular emphasis on the total lifetime costs. The administrations must be continuously supplied with qualified personnel in order to be able to safeguard investment activities in a responsible manner

[2881] Measures to recruit and retain employees with special expertise are discussed in more detail in chapter

[2882] Real estate, buildings and facilities investments should provide a balanced and cost-effective composition of the fixed asset base in relation to future needs

[2883] Not least, these needs will be affected by the continued restructuring of the Norwegian Defence Forces

[2884] Maintaining a sufficient level of investment that reduces the need for operation and maintenance in the long term is the key to overall cost savings for properties, buildings and facilities

[2885] The lowest possible lifetime costs are therefore an important goal for investments in property, buildings and structures

[2886] New, modern buildings generally have far better quality and standards than buildings built in the 1950s and 1960s

[2887] Replacement buildings for old and obsolete building stock and modernization will therefore provide a more maintenance-friendly building stock

[2888] The Armed Forces' buildings and facilities must have a similar standard to other, comparable public buildings and facilities, and comply with laws, rules and regulations for health, the environment and safety

[2889] The development of a balanced and cost-effective real estate stock will depend on, among other things: reduction of building stock and overcapacity utilization of spare capacity through consolidation in owned building stock flexible utilization of buildings performance standards of buildings joint use with other public and private enterprises need for new construction versus modernization local tax level

[2890] An annual rolling long-term plan will be prepared for the Armed Forces' property, building and civil engineering investments, prioritizing projects within a time perspective of 6 years

[2891] The plan will include both investment needs and operation and maintenance needs

[2892] It will be based on the amount of area for different building types with a uniform purpose

[2893] The plan will also be a tool for assessing whether it is possible to reduce the extent of building areas

[2894] Operation and maintenance of equipment, property, buildings and facilities belong to the largest expense categories on the operating side

[2895] To achieve the goals and achieve the reprioritizations that this report indicates, it is important to achieve operational savings within these categories

[2896] Calculations indicate significant savings potential in relation to materials management, primarily through the introduction of new technology and improved logistics processes

[2897] The work of mapping efficiency, savings potential and measures in the Armed Forces' materiel management is gathered under one umbrella

[2898] A strategy is being developed to improve the Armed Forces' logistics processes within materiel procurement, supply and storage, transport, maintenance, scrapping and disposal of materiel

[2899] Using modern methods and tools, this strategy will create the conditions for the best possible support for military operations through effective preparation and resource utilization in peacetime

[2900] This requires, among other things, increased coordination between the branches of defense and better coordination between military and civilian authorities within the Total Defense

[2901] The assessment of the administration's tasks and organization should be able to help identify savings potential

[2902] Strategies and measures will also be developed that can contribute to better coordinated logistics between the branches of defence

[2903] Concrete goals are being developed while a simple system of goal and performance indicators is being built

[2904] The following principles will be used as a basis for the logistics processes: concentration of logistics resources, but with the ability to disperse and reallocate coordination of the defence branches' purchasing, storage, distribution and maintenance purchasing of civilian services when this is more profitable than their own production, and sale of services when the Defence has the expertise and is competitive joint supply bases that carry out maintenance activities for departments from all defence branches reduced error rates and response times through the use/choice of technology and simplification of repairs changed and more centralised warehouse structure revenue financing of workshops and warehouse functions

[2905] Expenses/income from phasing out equipment must be included in the service life considerations in connection with equipment procurement

[2906] The equipment must be designed so that it does not trigger unnecessary costs or problems related to environmental regulations

[2907] Phasing out large systems or a large number of units must be considered holistically, so that a cost-effective dismantling of all elements is achieved simultaneously

[2908] Real estate, construction and facilities

[2909] The value of properties, buildings and facilities must be maintained through proper management, operation and maintenance

[2910] A goal for the period 1999-2002 is to achieve operational reductions without weakening maintenance standards

[2911] Streamlining operations and reducing land use are important tools in this work

[2912] Investments, operations and maintenance in property, buildings and facilities mutually influence each other

[2913] These factors must therefore be viewed in context to find the most cost-effective solutions in a long-term perspective

[2914] For example, new investments in modern and contemporary buildings can result in reduced operating costs

[2915] In other cases, it may be more economical to accept somewhat higher operating and maintenance costs for a limited period of time in order to avoid new investments

[2916] Investments have recently been made to centralize and improve storage conditions for materials

[2917] These investments often result in significant savings on materials, but increased operating costs for properties, buildings and facilities

[2918] The decisive factor is whether the investments are profitable for the Armed Forces overall

[2919] Further restructuring of the Armed Forces will, to the greatest extent possible, take place by removing entire units or departments from the structure so that the number of garrisons, bases and stations is reduced

[2920] This should reduce the Armed Forces' overall land requirements

[2921] Furthermore, the departments must prioritize strictly necessary buildings

[2922] Joint solutions and concentration of activities must be sought

[2923] Military activities continue at some of the Norwegian Armed Forces' fortifications

[2924] As the owner, the Armed Forces have the responsibility for the management of these national cultural monuments

[2925] This should not, however, prevent us from assessing whether, in specific cases, it would be profitable to close down or relocate current operations and, if necessary, only retain a minimal workforce to fulfill management responsibilities

[2926] In order to reduce land use and make the best possible use of the Armed Forces' property, activities must be consolidated and compressed

[2927] In addition, the useful life of buildings and structures can in some cases be increased by changing their use and extraordinary efforts at maintenance

[2928] This could reduce the demand for new buildings and facilities

[2929] Disposal of properties, buildings and structures will contribute to achieving the goal of area reductions

[2930] This reduces the need for funds for operation and maintenance

[2931] The reductions shall particularly occur through the phasing out/disposal of excess, obsolete and maintenance-intensive real estate

[2932] Energy conservation and other operational-saving measures will free up funds for maintenance

[2933] The same applies when activities are concentrated in owned buildings with available capacity and leases are terminated

[2934] Measures to safeguard health, environment and safety will overall be able to result in long-term operational reductions, although such measures may also in some cases lead to increases in area

[2935] Changing requirements for health, environment and safety, comfort, organizational changes and new materials will often require major changes throughout the life cycle of the buildings

[2936] In some cases, it will therefore be appropriate to have managed decay instead of full maintenance

[2937] Such a process does not, of course, prevent compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements

[2938] In a mobilisation defence, the development and maintenance of the force structure, as well as the ability to carry out mobilisation, is the most important and defining factor for the organisation and operation of the Armed Forces in peacetime

[2939] In addition, the Armed Forces shall ensure the assertion of sovereignty, the exercise of authority, international operations and other peacetime tasks

[2941] However, operational efficiency and responsiveness will vary in different parts of the organization

[2942] The peacekeeping organization must be restructured as a result of changes in the force structure and peacetime tasks

[2943] Restructuring the peacekeeping organization will contribute to achieving the overall goals for the structure and activities of the Armed Forces by freeing up resources

[2944] The organization and activities of the Armed Forces in peacetime must at all times have built-in flexibility for changes resulting from, among other things, security policy and economic developments and uncertainty

[2945] Overall and long-term planning is nevertheless of great importance in ensuring the most stable and targeted development of the organization

[2946] Military presence and visibility are necessary to assert Norwegian sovereignty in peacetime

[2950] Cost-effective solutions can lie across defense branches and weapons sectors

[2951] To achieve overall savings through organizational changes, it is also necessary to view different resources (personnel, materials, property, buildings and facilities) in context

[2952] Experience shows that significant operational reductions through organizational changes can primarily be achieved by reducing the number of service locations

[3111] International operations Our international engagement must be integrated as closely as possible with the Armed Forces' other activities and structure

[3112] Forces intended for a role in international operations should thus be organized as similarly as possible to other units in the force structure

[3113] Likewise, expertise for and expertise from international efforts must be integrated as an important part of the Armed Forces' overall competence building

[3114] Future readiness forces for international operations will be organized as reaction forces, reinforcement forces and follow-up forces, respectively

[3115] The reaction forces are small, high-quality units that can be quickly deployed into a conflict area to establish a presence

[3116] Reinforcement forces should be able to expand an established engagement, either in terms of scope or specialization

[3117] These have significantly longer reaction times

[3118] The follow-up forces should make it possible to maintain an established commitment over time

[3119] In the case of the Army, it is primarily standing units and units that have been trained together during initial service that may be relevant as reaction forces

[3120] There is no intention to establish reinforcement forces, but it may be an option to upgrade follow-up forces to reinforcement forces when conditions are right

[3121] The emergency forces shall be an integrated part of the national defense structure

[3122] The bulk of the Army's contribution will in the future be established within the framework of a brigade

[3123] The brigade will become a resource well for materiel, and in the long term also for personnel

[3124] The Telemark Battalion is planned as part of such a brigade

[3125] By using the brigade's deployment plans, ad hoc establishment of departments for individual missions can be avoided

[3126] The new organization will also provide operational benefits through simplified materiel administration and more jointly trained units, and will create better conditions for returning expertise to the rest of the Armed Forces

[3127] The development of such a brigade as a framework for the Army's international contribution is still some way off

[3128] The Navy's and Air Force's contributions to international operations will largely be based on the units that are currently registered with NATO's response forces and the UN system

[3129] However, certain additions and adjustments will be considered

[3130] Because the contributions are primarily based on standing units, most of the units will be able to react quickly and gain the status of reaction forces

[3131] A fundamental prerequisite for all efforts is that appropriate contractual arrangements are established that ensure the participation of a sufficient number of personnel

[3132] The departments earmarked for international operations will receive the additional equipment that is necessary

[3133] Great importance is placed on the safety of personnel

[3134] The best possible protection of our military forces abroad, for example against the possible use of weapons of mass destruction, will be of greater importance for planning

[3135] Emphasis will be placed on the fact that the additional material can also have useful value in the national defense structure

[3137] Environmental considerations The Armed Forces' planning and development shall promote environmental safety

[3138] The Armed Forces shall protect the environment on an equal footing with society at large, and ensure that considerations of assigned tasks are balanced against environmental impacts

[3139] The Armed Forces' work on environmental security shall contribute to creating and preserving peace and security, and to reducing environmental threats with possible impacts on Norway

[3140] Environmental work should be an underlying factor in the work to ensure that the Armed Forces have trained personnel, functional materiel and timely establishments at all times

[3141] The measures must be designed so that existing environmental problems are reduced and new environmental problems are prevented, cf. chapter

[3142] The Armed Forces must gain better overview and control of their impact on the environment

[3143] Attitude-building work at all levels is important in this context

[3144] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 Investigating the consequences of restructuring measures, as well as developing measures and requirements for environmentally sound solutions, will be central to environmental work in the period

[3145] The following aspects must be emphasized in the investigations

[3146] new or changed challenges in relation to civil society integrated environmental requirements in the specifications of new weapons and systems new or changed environmental requirements in connection with allied exercises and Norwegian participation in international operations better mapping of areas and objects that the Armed Forces must take into account better mapping of the impacts

[3147] Of the Armed Forces' training activities The Armed Forces must comply with environmental requirements to prevent occupational injuries and protect against accidents and incidents in the workplace

[3148] At the same time, appropriate installations and establishments for daily operations and effective education and training must be ensured

[3149] Measures to comply with environmental requirements must be implemented in a planned and cost-effective manner to achieve satisfactory environmental quality at the lowest cost

[3150] A management tool for management, control and reporting of environmental protection work will be introduced

[3151] Furthermore, the aim is to build more targeted expertise for environmental protection officers and improve the integration of environmental protection measures into the planning and budget system

[3152] Preventive environmental protection can save the Armed Forces from future cleanup efforts

[3153] The Armed Forces must exploit the opportunities that exist to reduce unwanted impacts on the environment and adopt environmentally friendly technology where possible

[3154] Life-cycle considerations must be the basis for all decisions about new activities, new equipment and new infrastructure

[3155] This means that the Defence's project management system must be expanded to include life-cycle environmental considerations, that education and training must integrate environmental considerations, and that a reporting system must be developed that makes the objectives, results and costs of the measures visible

[3156] Clean-up of environmental problems must be carried out efficiently and at the lowest possible cost

[3157] Prioritization between different measures must be based on environmental risk assessments

[3158] This requires the development of methods for measuring costs, efficiency and environmental quality

[3159] Bi- and multilateral environmental cooperation with other countries' defense authorities must be further developed

[3160] Research and development (R&D

[3162] This activity shall support the overall defense planning, selection of operational and technical solutions, and the implementation of the Armed Forces' projects

[3163] The Norwegian Armed Forces' own research and development agencies shall concentrate their activities in areas where the Norwegian Armed Forces' needs cannot be met in an appropriate manner by others

[3244] Long-term challenges

[3245] Defence planning requires a long-term perspective to further develop and maintain the Defence Forces' structure and expertise in an efficient and targeted manner

[3246] Although the long-term cost estimates are highly uncertain, the calculations nevertheless reveal a fundamental question

[3247] Maintaining our defense - as we know it today - towards the year 2020 will require a higher level of funding for defense purposes in five to ten years

[3248] Above all, we must further develop a balanced defense

[3249] This means that the tasks of the Armed Forces, the structure and activities of the Armed Forces, and the resources for defense purposes must be in harmony with each other

[3250] If the policy in this report is to be continued in the coming decade, a moderate, annual real growth of about ½ percent is required

[3251] Although this course will continue to lead to a decline in the defense budget's share of gross domestic product, the Armed Forces will still be able to fulfill its tasks in the coming decade

[3252] If we are unable to continue the transformation at the necessary pace and extent, or if available resources become less than expected over time, the problems with maintaining a well-dimensioned defense will be exacerbated

[3253] The most obvious consequences of such a development are major misinvestments since the investment funds to supplement all the deficiencies in the power structure are not available

[3254] Failing prerequisites will very easily result in an unbalanced defense with a weakened ability to solve the many tasks assigned to the Armed Forces

[3255] This could lead to us running a greater security risk than before, for example if the ability for national invasion defense is weakened

[3256] In that case, we will become dependent on extensive reinforcement support from our allies before a major crisis or military conflict

[3257] A surprise military attack in such a situation would cause the Norwegian Defence Forces to collapse immediately

[3258] Therefore, such a solution could only be acceptable as a result of agreements on extensive division of labor and specialization within the alliance, which take special account of Norway's geographical location

[3259] We will expose ourselves to a similar - but in many ways even greater - security risk if we are forced towards a defense based on the long-standing

[3280] Conscription In recent years, several countries in Europe have completely or partially abolished conscription

[3281] This is related to, among other things, force reductions and changed requirements for the forces as a result of increased emphasis on international operations

[3282] To continue our nationally balanced defense, however, we have too few inhabitants, and the country is too large, for us to transition to a professional defense in Norway

[3283] A conscription defense system greatly benefits from the soldiers' knowledge from civilian life and has an important integrating function in our society

[3284] The principle of general conscription is therefore firmly established in government policy

[3285] This does not mean that military service should be carried out in exactly the same way as before

[3286] The conscription system must first and foremost provide the Armed Forces with conscripted personnel in the necessary numbers and ensure adequate education

[3287] But in order to satisfactorily carry out the Armed Forces' tasks in the future, the conscription system must be assessed and developed regularly to capture new developments in society, within military technology and within military operations

[3288] As part of the work on the long-term report, the government has therefore placed emphasis on assessing the content of conscription

[3289] The history of conscription was given a broad overview in Parliamentary Proposal No. 98 (1991-92), and the Storting agreed to the changes in service time and pattern that were proposed in the proposal

[3290] In addition, further changes to military conscription have been adopted

[3291] A principle of continuous service has been introduced, the service pattern in the Army and Air Force has been adjusted, and the conscription reserve has been discontinued

[3292] Furthermore, the Storting has agreed that the studies to assess community service should not be continued

[3293] These changes have helped shape the current conscription system

[3294] Many people associate conscription only with conscripted personnel

[3295] Officers who leave the Armed Forces at working age are also subject to military service

[3296] Since conscripted officers constitute a special and limited part of those subject to conscription, this group is discussed separately

[3306] The conscription scheme must be designed to take into account a number of important considerations

[3307] These are discussed below

[3308] Consideration of justice

[3309] The principle of general military service is stated in Section 109 of the Constitution

[3310] Every citizen of the state is generally equally obliged, for a certain period of time, to protect his Fatherland, regardless of birth or wealth

[3311] Special arrangements

[3314] The state can thus basically require any citizen to serve military service

[3315] The constitution does not require everyone to perform military service

[3316] It is not the consideration of the individual that is decisive, but the consideration of the state's interests

[3317] For example, personnel with socially important tasks have been exempted from military service and mobilization

[3318] Although the idea of an “equal” and “fair” military service thus gained traction in 1814, the exceptions at that time were still very extensive

[3319] It took over 60 years before the principle of universal conscription, equal for all, was practiced fairly

[3320] The Constitution's principle of equality has played a relatively modest role in the political debate, in legislative drafting and in case law

[3321] And when the principle of equality is referred to, there is some ambiguity as to whether the principle implies the rule more than the exception

[3322] This may be because the requirement for equality can be viewed from different perspectives

[3323] Equality or justice is based on the principle that equal cases should be treated equally

[3324] However, it can be problematic to determine the criteria for equality in a given situation

[3325] For example, emphasis can be placed on giving or taking the same amount from each, or the allocation can be made randomly, for example by drawing lots

[3326] To determine who would serve in military service, drawing lots was previously used in Norway during the interwar period

[3327] This selection method is used today in Denmark

[3328] There is no definitive answer to what constitutes a "fair" conscription system

[3329] In a democracy, the decisive factor must be that a broad majority of the population perceives the conscription system as fair

[3330] Broad support for conscription is necessary to maintain the will to defend on which total defense is based

[3331] In order to safeguard the interests of justice, the government therefore sees it as crucial that all able-bodied men continue to be called up for initial service, and that the total service time for all those serving conscription is as equal in duration as possible

[3332] The detailed rules for implementing military service are determined by law

[3333] Today, there are five laws that regulate military and civilian service

[3334] This legislation was adopted at a time when the security policy situation was very different from today

[3335] Furthermore, the legislation does not provide the desired clarity and transparency overall

[3336] The "Legal Structure Committee" proposed a closer assessment of whether laws on military and civilian service should be merged

[3337] This proposal has so far been followed up to a limited extent

[3338] The Ministry of Defence will therefore take the initiative to assess the appropriateness of replacing the current legislation in this area

[3339] Our defense concept is based on several principles

[3340] General military service is one of these

[3341] The tasks of the Armed Forces must be carried out within these frameworks; this also applies to new or changed tasks

[3342] If it is not possible to solve a task based on military service, we must either refrain from solving the task, solve the task with greater risk, or further develop the arrangements that supplement traditional military service

[3343] Technological developments are leading to more advanced military equipment and enabling higher tempo and intensity of operations

[3344] New military operational concepts emphasize exploiting these opportunities to conduct more effective operations

[3345] This also applies to the new Norwegian operational concept discussed in the chapter

[3346] This concept places great demands on initiative and speed at all levels and on personnel with high competence and training standards at all levels

[3347] In recent years, an increasing number of increasingly demanding international operations have been initiated and carried out

[3348] The forces that will participate in such operations must therefore be prepared for varying challenges

[3349] The requirements for competence among commanders and crews at all levels are increasing in line with this development

[3350] The experience with Norwegian conscripts is good, and the departments consistently maintain a satisfactory training standard

[3351] Through targeted education, training and practice, it will be possible to meet the vast majority of competence needs with conscripted personnel

[3352] The majority of the private crew will therefore continue to be conscripted personnel in the future

[3353] The above-mentioned developments may nevertheless indicate a greater proportion of temporarily employed crews in certain areas

[3354] Departments staffed with contract civilian personnel will be able to be ready for asserting sovereignty, crisis management and international operations more quickly than departments staffed with only conscript personnel

[3355] However, costs will increase if conscripts are replaced with contract personnel

[3356] In the current situation, the government therefore does not find it necessary to advocate a scheme where entire departments are set up with contract personnel

[3357] If in the long term it turns out that developments are not compatible with such a guideline, the government will reconsider the issue

[3358] In terms of quality, it is possible to achieve better mobilization departments, among other things, by making adjustments to the current management of the mobilization defense

[3359] Firstly, personnel who have completed their initial service in the same department should be transferred to the same department in the mobilization deployments

[3360] This will reduce the time it takes to prepare the unit for a mobilization phase compared to the current system where soldiers are placed in mobilization formations more individually

[3361] However, such a change in routines must still accommodate the need for exemption schemes for socially important tasks and provide the opportunity to utilize civilian expertise acquired after initial service

[3362] Secondly, the time that the individual soldier is in the mobilization formations should be reduced

[3363] In this way, the youngest and most recently trained personnel are consistently utilized in the deployments, while the oldest personnel will be transferred to the war reserve at an earlier time than today

[3364] Such a reduction in the time available must be balanced against the number of crews trained each year

[3365] International operations Norway does not use crews under the Conscription Act for demanding international operations

[3366] The crews in such operations are temporary employees, and the service is based on volunteerism

[3367] However, this scheme is based on the crews' basic military training from their initial service

[3368] In the government's view, requirements resulting from Norwegian participation in international operations should therefore be included in the training of conscripts, especially for those who are initially eligible for such service

[3371] Most have completed three years of upper secondary school

[3372] The general knowledge of conscripts is therefore relatively high compared to countries with professional defense

[3386] The service therefore represents mutual competence building for both the Armed Forces and the conscripts

[3395] However, most conscripts are most easily available during the summer intake in the year in which they have completed high school

To meet the Armed Forces' need for continuity and operability, the principle of distributing call-ups throughout the year is maintained

[3587] SUMMARY - THE GOVERNMENT'S OVERALL POLICY

[3588] FOR CONSERVATION A comprehensive policy for conscription must consider the overarching considerations in context

[3589] In order to safeguard the interests of efficiency and fairness, the government considers it essential that all able-bodied men continue to be called up for initial service, and that the total period of service is as equal in duration as possible

[3590] The criteria for serviceability have been adjusted so that more people can be called up for service

[3591] The Armed Forces must at all times base themselves on utilizing the number of personnel available, and establish systems for education and deployment that are flexible enough to accommodate variations in, among other things, the size of the cohorts

[3592] Changed tasks and framework conditions increase the Defence's requirements for competence

[3593] The government believes that it will also be possible in the future to meet all ordinary competence needs related to the Armed Forces' tasks through general military service

[3594] The Government therefore does not find it necessary in the current situation to advocate a scheme where entire departments are set up with contract personnel

[3595] Nevertheless, supplementary schemes are still required to address special skills needs

[3596] The government's goal is to develop solutions that satisfy the needs of the Armed Forces while at the same time safeguarding the interests and needs of conscripts

[3597] The Government will facilitate the best possible dialogue between conscripts and the authorities

[3598] The time between session and distribution should be shortened, and factors such as co-determination, predictability and flexibility should be emphasized in the development of the conscription system

[3599] Through conscription, the Armed Forces must utilize the available civilian expertise, while at the same time facilitating the development of expertise that can benefit the individual and civil society

[3600] The Government will continue the goals that military service should not require more than one year of study, and that soldiers should not graduate into unemployment

[3601] The Ministry will continue to work on solutions that make it possible to call crews into service when they are most readily available

[3602] For those who are invited and have also been offered a place at educational institutions, emphasis is placed on utilizing guaranteed schemes for permanent study places

[3603] In order to meet the Armed Forces' need for continuity and operability, the Ministry sees it as problematic to change the current distribution of calls throughout the year

[3604] However, the Ministry will continue to work on assessing the number of calls and the timing of calls against the disadvantages this entails, especially in relation to school and working life

[3605] The Ministry of Defence will take the initiative to assess the appropriateness of replacing the current legislation regulating military and civilian service obligations

[3606] The government is also planning to adjust the current appointment system as a result of new needs

Personnel policy In light of the increasing personnel turnover in the Armed Forces, the Storting decided on 7 May 1997 that a report should be presented to the Storting on the personnel situation in the Armed Forces

[3608] The Storting's decision was as follows

[3609] The Storting requests that the Government submit a report by the end of 1997 in which all aspects of the critical personnel situation in the Armed Forces are assessed in an overall analysis, and in which short-term and long-term measures to resolve these challenges/problems are put forward

[3610] On the basis that the Ministry wanted to present a long-term report on the activities of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002, and in it would provide a comprehensive presentation of the personnel situation and the personnel policy that the Ministry will base itself on in the years to come, it was found appropriate to raise with the Presidency of the Storting whether the Storting could agree not to present a separate personnel report

[3611] On the basis of a response from the Presidency of 4 December 1997 and consultations in the Defence Committee, the Ministry decided not to present a separate personnel report, but rather to provide a relatively concrete description of personnel policy in the long-term report

[3612] The Ministry has chosen to follow up on the Storting's decision by explaining in this long-term report the personnel situation and what measures the Ministry is considering implementing to stem unwanted staff turnover

[3613] It is assumed that the specific measures implemented are in accordance with the state's overall wage and personnel policy, and that implementation takes place within the overall wage and bargaining system, or pursuant to authorization from the Ministry of Labor and Administration

[3614] Solving the Armed Forces' tasks in peace, crisis and war places high demands on the personnel in the organization

[3615] The need for both cutting-edge expertise, continuity and experience is increasing as a result of, among other things, new technology, a new military operational concept and restructuring of the business

[3616] The Armed Forces have long traditions of good leadership and personnel management, but the organization must also utilize new ideas and new knowledge to further develop this expertise

[3617] An expansive labor market presents the Armed Forces with challenges in the personnel area, both in terms of recruitment and measures to stop excessive attrition in parts of the organization

[3618] The Armed Forces must be prepared for this development to continue in the years to come

[3619] The Ministry emphasizes that personnel policy in the Armed Forces is designed so that qualified personnel remain in the organization

[3620] A good personnel policy is based on the staff's understanding of the company's challenges, goals and tasks; conscious development and use of staff; the exercise of timely leadership; and good working conditions and a good working environment

[3621] A comprehensive personnel policy must therefore be designed in which the various elements and challenges are seen in context based on a contemporary management philosophy

[3622] The overall objective of personnel policy is to have a highly motivated personnel corps with sufficient expertise to carry out the Defence's tasks

[3623] The means to achieve this objective will be: forward-looking personnel planning targeted recruitment strategy making the Armed Forces competitive overall by also emphasizing factors other than salary broad investment in competence development emphasis on family policy measures active gender equality policy

[3624] In the previous four-year period, personnel reductions have been a key tool for achieving operational savings

[3625] Personnel reductions are still necessary, and the main lines of the restructuring policy, with an emphasis on restructuring under security, remain unchanged

[3626] As a result of the Armed Forces' management concept, the Ministry of Defence's personnel policy role has changed, from assuming relatively direct and executive responsibility to establishing more general guidelines for the Armed Forces' military organization and the civilian agencies

[3627] This development will continue in the coming four-year period through further delegation of executive functions and a stronger focus on linking and implementing the government's overall personnel policy

[3628] STRATEGIC PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT Competition for expertise in society will likely continue to increase in the years ahead

[3629] The employees are the Armed Forces' most important resource

[3630] How well the Armed Forces succeed in attracting, retaining and developing a workforce with the necessary qualifications is crucial to the organization's quality and results

[3631] Strategic personnel management is therefore a key concept in the design of personnel policy

[3632] Traditional management of employees must be supplemented with measures for recruitment, development and management of human resources in line with overall and holistic goals

[3633] An overall strategy for the management, control and development of human resources must therefore be developed

[3634] Important areas and measures will be

[3635] development and use of new systems for personnel planning targeted recruitment strategy

[3636] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 increased emphasis on career planning continuation of the work on management and development of the Armed Forces' competence systems for job assessment, analysis, description and structure as a basis for salary structure flexible salary policy management development and management selection family and equality policy health, environment and safety

[3637] The Norwegian Armed Forces High Command has begun work on designing a new personnel strategy

[3638] This will be based on the Armed Forces' values and consist of strategic plans for career and reward, competence, family policy, management and health, environment and safety

[3639] The Armed Forces' civilian agencies shall develop corresponding strategies adapted to their own circumstances

[3640] CONTINUING THE CONVERSION

[3641] The Norwegian Armed Forces, with its 25,000 employees, is one of the country's largest employers

[3642] Throughout the post-war period, the Armed Forces have been considered a secure workplace with a guarantee of lifelong employment

[3643] However, recent years have been characterized by restructuring and personnel reductions

[3644] The operating budget is largely linked to personnel costs

[3645] To achieve the necessary scale of operational savings, the previous long-term report called for extensive man-year reductions over a ten-year period

[3646] However, it has proven neither desirable nor possible to solve the tasks satisfactorily with such extensive personnel reductions

[3647] On the other hand, it is not possible to protect investments and make necessary reprioritizations on the operational side without savings

[3648] The Ministry emphasizes that the Armed Forces must at all times have a personnel structure that is adapted to the organization and activities

[3649] Staff reductions alone are not sufficient to achieve the necessary operational savings

[3650] However, staff reductions are still necessary, but at a slower pace and to a lesser extent than previously planned

[3651] The main lines of today's policy for the personnel side of the restructuring will continue to be guiding

[3652] This means that layoffs should be avoided as far as possible

[3653] Redundant personnel should be offered retraining and skills development that can qualify them for other positions in the Armed Forces, in the rest of the state administration or in the labor market in general

[3654] The individual redundant person should be able to be given an adequate job offer while the person is still in the line organization

[3655] The resource organization has been a very important element in the personnel restructuring

[3656] With the significant organizational changes that will come in the years ahead, the Ministry believes that the Resource Organization should continue to exist

[3657] However, the organization should be able to be adapted to the current needs, and closer coordination of resources with the line organization should be considered

[3658] It should also be considered whether the expertise that the Resource Organization has acquired can be used in more areas

[3659] The Armed Forces have a number of measures to promote retirement and mobility that, in the Ministry's view, mainly cover the need for instruments in this area

[3660] However, it is desirable to look more closely at how mobility can be improved for civilian employees

[3661] Work is underway to design measures that can stimulate relocation beyond the mandatory relocation requirement

[3662] Greater mobility will be beneficial both for the Armed Forces and for the individual employee

[3663] Restructuring and staff reductions can have a negative impact, not only on those affected, but also on those remaining and on recruitment

[3664] The Ministry therefore places emphasis on highlighting the positive effects of the restructuring

[3665] The Norwegian Armed Forces should appear as a modern employer that can offer challenging and safe workplaces where high demands are placed on the individual's competence

[3666] The employee organizations have contributed to the restructuring process in a very constructive way

[3667] Further restructuring efforts are highly dependent on the participation of employee organizations

[3668] The Ministry therefore emphasizes continued close and good cooperation between employers and employee organizations at all levels of the Armed Forces

[3669] In this context, it is essential that the restructuring takes place in accordance with law and agreements

[3670] MEASURES TO KEEP ADDITIONAL PAY AT A HIGH LEVEL

[3671] The need for highly qualified employees is increasing, while important personnel groups are leaving the Defence at an excessive pace

[3672] This leads to the loss of important expertise that takes a long time to replace

[3678] This competence can only be acquired through the Armed Forces' own educational institutions and through the experience the officers gain through their service

[3702] The Bjønnes I and Bjønnes II committees

[3703] Due to the fact that the Armed Forces were constantly losing personnel with high expertise who were difficult to replace, an internal party-composed committee was established, the Bjønnes II Committee

[3704] The committee was tasked with preparing proposals on how the Armed Forces should meet the challenges of an expansive labor market

[3705] Previously, the so-called Bjønnes I Committee had looked at personnel matters related to the pilot situation in the Armed Forces

[3706] Some of the proposals from the Bjønnes committees have already been implemented

[3707] The Bjønnes II Committee has conducted analyses of casual departures, that is, all departures other than retirements, both in the military organization of the Armed Forces and in the civilian agencies

[3708] The analyses showed that the random departure has been increasing in the last two years, see table

[3715] The personnel shortage in the Armed Forces is primarily evident in information technology, electronics, certain technical groups, administration and finance

[3716] But the operational sector is also experiencing increasing attrition, so that the personnel shortage tends to be pervasive in most areas within the Armed Forces

[3717] About 80 percent of those who have quit are in the 30-40 year age group

[3718] The committee has conducted two large surveys to map the reasons why civilian and military employees leave

[3719] One survey was aimed at those who have left the Armed Forces within the last two years, while the other was aimed at those who are still employed by the organization

[3720] A total of around 1,600 interviews were conducted

[3721] The results showed that the reasons why military personnel leave are family considerations, lack of career opportunities and financial circumstances

[3722] The most important reasons for resignation among civil servants are financial circumstances, lack of career opportunities and the desire to try something new

[3723] There was good agreement between both surveys in the view of which areas the Armed Forces should concentrate on in personnel policy

[3724] Both those who have left and those who are employed highlight salary as the most important area for improvement in personnel policy

[3725] Better salary conditions, on the other hand, are unlikely to be enough alone to counteract the loss of key personnel in the Armed Forces

[3726] Both military and civilian veterans believe there is a need to prioritize family policy measures

[3727] The studies also indicate that there is a need for a comprehensive personnel policy effort that focuses on better systems and possibly other criteria for remuneration, better facilitation of career paths, better systems for selecting and recruiting managers, and changes in the command system

[3728] The surveys also showed that a full 77 percent of military employees wanted to separate rank and salary

[3729] Furthermore, 63 percent of military and civilian employees believed that opportunities for personal remuneration must be provided

[3730] Many also expressed frustration with the restructuring process and that tasks and resources were not in proportion to each other

[3731] However, well-being and the working environment in the Armed Forces are consistently described as very good by both the military and civilian parts of the personnel

[3732] Based on the surveys, the committee's proposals were mainly aimed at finances, family policy and career-related measures in both the short and long term

[3733] The committee's main conclusion is that the Armed Forces must have a comprehensive personnel policy

In the area of family policy, it is proposed, among other things, to increase the number of benefit trips for commuters; expand the relocation bonus agreement; the right to leave in all public sector activities for spouses/cohabitants who move with them due to an order; develop a strategy to secure job offers for spouses, and establish scholarship schemes for spouses/cohabitants for further education purposes

[3737] It is also worth noting that the committee recommends equal treatment of civilians and military personnel when the conditions between these groups are comparable

[3760] DEFENCE SALARY POLICY

[3761] The work of designing a wage policy platform in the Armed Forces, as recommended by the Central Government Collective Agreement, has not been finalized between the negotiating parties

[3762] In the department's view, this is unfortunate because the wage policy cannot be used in a targeted enough manner in the effort to recruit and retain qualified employees

[3763] Until now, the Armed Forces, like the rest of the state, has had a salary policy practice that is mainly based on the principle of equality

[3764] The Ministry assesses the labor market situation to the point that it is necessary to provide somewhat greater scope for individual wage differences in the organization

[3765] This requires a system with clear and fair criteria

[3766] Such a system could include job evaluation, personal remuneration and market considerations

[3767] Today, one can find examples of large wage disparities between civilian and military employees with roughly similar work tasks and qualifications

[3768] Biases in favor of military employees have in some cases led to transfers to civilian positions in the Defense Department to perform roughly the same tasks

[3769] The establishment of a salary policy must therefore strive for harmonization of salary and working conditions between civilian and military employees where this is appropriate

[3770] The Ministry also sees it as natural that different contractual arrangements for civilians and military personnel be coordinated where the conditions are comparable

[3771] The local wage negotiations in the Armed Forces are re- St report no

[3774] For the Workshop Agreement, negotiations are conducted centrally, and based on the Workshop Agreement's special mechanisms, this is still assumed to be appropriate

[3775] There should be a greater distinction between degree and salary

[3776] In principle, the degree should express the necessary level of command, while salary is linked more to the individual position's area of responsibility and work, the position holder's competence and an assessment of the market in general with regard to the salary and working conditions of different groups

[3777] When officers serve in local, training departments with a high level of activity, they often receive high income as a result of salary and variable allowances

[3778] Often this applies to the younger commanding officer

[3779] When officers later in their careers enter staff positions or other positions that do not trigger activity-based supplements, income development often becomes negative

[3780] This raises questions about whether income development should be smoothed out throughout a career

[3781] However, this undermines, and must be weighed against, the principles that grade and placement in the salary frame/salary range are standardized based on the importance and responsibility of the position, and that service beyond the normal working day should be compensated individually according to specified rules

[3782] The Armed Forces have traditionally been cautious about using the wage-related instruments that the Main Tariff Agreement and the Workshop Agreement provide opportunities for

[3783] However, increased competition for labour has made it necessary to use most of the instruments authorized by the Main Collective Agreement in the state
