[3890] Information Technology in the Armed Forces

[3891] INTRODUCTION Over the years, the Norwegian Armed Forces have acquired and developed a number of electronically based information systems

[3892] Such information systems are used in military operations and in the ongoing operations of the organization, and the systems include both telecommunications and computer systems

[3893] However, many of the Armed Forces' systems overlap

[3894] The systems are rarely based on the war organization's overall need for information, but are often aimed at individual areas of daily operations

[3895] The information on the force structure is not good enough, and the management information for the Armed Forces' activities in peacetime is therefore insufficient

[3896] In addition, the Armed Forces' many information systems have been developed for use on various types of technical equipment

[3897] In practice, the total defense perspective has been given little weight in the development of military and civilian information systems

[3898] Planned utilization of society's overall resources within the total defense concept requires extensive cooperation and exchange of information

[3899] The need for coordination between the Armed Forces and civil emergency preparedness is therefore indisputable

[3900] Coordination and prioritization of the Armed Forces' resources must be based on a common understanding of the Armed Forces' tasks and activities in peace, crisis and war

[3901] The IT initiatives in the Armed Forces have not so far been implemented within a comprehensive framework

[3902] In some cases, the technology itself has been given disproportionate importance

[3903] The Armed Forces have also not had good enough strategies, plans and instruments to meet the need for expertise in the IT area

[3904] In the years to come, it is necessary for the Armed Forces to develop and retain such expertise

[3905] Despite the fact that the Armed Forces spend significant funds on information technology, the Armed Forces' information systems have not so far contributed enough to increasing the efficiency of operations

[3906] This gives good reason to maintain a critical focus on the continued IT investment in the Armed Forces

[3907] The rapid technological development provides sta

[3908] you new opportunities to better solve the Armed Forces' tasks

[3909] To take full advantage of these opportunities, goals, organization, expertise and technology must be seen in context

[3910] The use of information technology will therefore be central to the Armed Forces' restructuring

[3911] The Armed Forces must actively exploit the possibilities of technology to further develop effective military defense in peace, crisis and war

[3912] This must happen within the framework of the Total Defense and the alliance

[3913] Therefore, information technology is given special attention in this message

[3914] IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT TRENDS

[3915] Technological developments in civil electronics and information technology are expected to continue at a formidable pace

[3916] As mentioned in chapter 4.6, capacities double on average approximately every two years

[3917] This provides new opportunities and places new demands on both our civilian society and our military forces

[3918] The spread of information technology has occurred very rapidly, and today there is hardly any sector in society that is without electronic information systems

[3919] Increased use of information systems also makes many sectors of society dependent on the functioning of these systems

[3920] Another expression of the increased spread of information technology is the accelerating use of open, worldwide computer networks

[3921] This has led to growing awareness of the political and military challenges that this can create in certain situations, cf

[3922] Box 9.1 Operational management systems of the future

[3923] The use of information technology has great utility in connection with the management of military operations

[3924] After World War II, technological developments have made it possible to collect information of operational value in ever-new ways and on a far greater scale than before

[3925] Translating this information into a comprehensive situational understanding therefore represents a major challenge for the management apparatus in modern military forces

[3926] The Armed Forces already use information systems to support command and control of military operations

[3927] In the future, this type of system will be able to integrate all available information and present complete and updated situational pictures to the military command apparatus

[3928] Such systems will also be able to offer advanced forms of decision support, for example by estimating the outcome of alternative tactical maneuvers

[3929] Furthermore, management decisions and orders can be communicated via the same information systems all the way to the competing departments and units

[3930] This will allow operational management in the future to focus more on making the right decisions, while the collection and presentation of data, decision support and the transmission of orders are to a greater extent carried out by the information systems

[3932] We are moving towards a new reality where conflicts can be fought to a greater extent with the support of electronic aids

[3933] Attention to and capability for information warfare is increasing in a number of countries and organizations, cf

[3934] New management systems based on extensive use of information technology will affect military operations in a profound way

[3936] GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

[3937] The Armed Forces' use of information technology must, above all, meet the Armed Forces' needs for information

[3938] The focus of the Armed Forces' activities in peacetime is the production of the force structure

[3939] The overall requirements for information must therefore be based on the Armed Forces' tasks and overall force structure

[3940] To ensure efficient production, the information must reflect both the individual elements and the overall structure and activities of the Armed Forces

[3941] The establishment of the Armed Forces' overall war organization requires mobilization

[3942] Therefore, the connection between organization, personnel, material, property, buildings and facilities largely only exists "on paper

[3943] If this information is not complete, correct and consistent, or if the communication systems are not adequate, the war organization will not be able to be established as quickly as expected during mobilization

[3944] The Armed Forces' information needs can be roughly grouped based on the needs related to the management of the war organization and the peace organization, respectively

[3945] The leadership of the peace organization must be assured of information that provides both a comprehensive and sufficiently detailed overview of its activities in peace

[3946] This includes, among other things, goals, missions and plans for the development of the Armed Forces' force structure

[3947] For the management of military operations, all information that builds situational understanding and supports the management of the operations itself will be central

[3948] This requires information about the status of one's own forces, intelligence, climatic and geographical conditions, etc., and the ability to communicate with subordinate departments and units

[3949] In modern military operations, speed and initiative will be essential, cf. chapter

[3950] This places great demands on the information systems that are to facilitate the effective management of such operations in peace, crisis and war

[3951] Cooperation and collaboration

[3952] Norway's defense is based on the principle of total defense and allied support

[3953] It is therefore a prerequisite that the information systems in the Armed Forces must be able to exchange information with other parts of the Total Defence Force, our allies and international organizations

[3954] The degree of automation in such information exchange will, however

[3955] depend on agreed standards and must be balanced against cost considerations

[3956] The Government wishes to actively influence the formulation in 1997-98 of strategies and plans for information exchange, both nationally and internationally, to meet civilian as well as military needs

[3957] The Ministry of Defence must continuously decide in which national and international forums it is necessary to be represented with defence expertise

[3958] Concrete examples may include the development of joint command and control systems in NATO, planning for allied forces' use of our telecommunications and data networks when deployed in Norway, or participation in national and international standardization work

[3959] This commitment will help ensure that information can be exchanged in the best possible way

[3960] The Armed Forces must also be able to assess the consequences of increasing use of information technology on the civilian side in our own society, on the military side among our allies and among potential adversaries

[3961] The Government believes that all development of information systems should be seen in context, and managed and coordinated from a common perspective

[3962] To contribute to the necessary coordination within the Armed Forces, a set of comprehensive requirements for the Armed Forces' information systems will be developed

[3963] Information technology is also an important factor in the transformation of the Armed Forces

[3964] The Ministry will therefore prioritize initiatives that can make the Armed Forces more efficient as a whole

[3965] These initiatives must simultaneously address the needs of the defense branches and individual departments

[3966] To ensure that the Armed Forces develop effective systems, development must take place with a holistic perspective on another level as well

[3967] Focus must be placed on the connections between goals, organization, competence and technology

[3968] A one-sided technological focus will not succeed

[3969] Technology is only an aid for efficient handling of information

[3970] Introducing technical solutions without the users having or being given sufficient competence, or without the organization being adapted to the new work patterns, will have little positive, and perhaps even negative, effects

[3971] Development on the IT side must therefore be an integrated part of the Armed Forces' overall organizational development

[3972] Competence building The Armed Forces have not had good enough strategies, plans and instruments to meet the need for competence within the IT area

[3973] The Ministry will consider measures to better safeguard this

[3974] The understanding of the possibilities of information technology in the development of the Armed Forces must be strengthened

[3975] It is particularly important to build such understanding and expertise among the Armed Forces' leaders

[3976] Therefore, both the military academies and the Norwegian Armed Forces Staff College must contribute to the necessary competence development

[3977] However, the Armed Forces also need specialized strategic expertise and professional competence in the IT area

[3978] Measures that can help recruit and retain the necessary expertise are described in more detail in Chapter

[3979] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 Vulnerability and security As society's dependence on electronic information systems increases, the need to protect these systems in a responsible manner also increases

[3980] Functions such as banking and finance, energy supply, telecommunications, transportation, water supply and petroleum production will become very vulnerable if, for example, sensitive information can be read or influenced by unauthorized persons from open computer networks

[3981] It is a goal that important information systems in society must function satisfactorily in peace as well as in crisis and war

[3982] The Armed Forces must work actively to ensure that these systems are developed and used in a safe and secure manner

[3983] The development of networks with many information providers and automated search and collation tools will increase the importance of comprehensive and strategic control over the dissemination of information

[3984] If necessary, such overall control must come at the expense of traditional, and more detailed, control

[3985] Reference is also made to the Storting's consideration of the Preventive Security Service Act

[3987] Standardization and reuse Standardization and reuse are becoming an increasingly important part of the work of developing information systems

[3988] Instead of completely tailoring new technical solutions, solutions that have already been developed in other contexts are being utilized to a greater extent

[3989] This can help reduce development time, development costs, and maintenance costs

[3990] In administrative areas, such reuse for the Armed Forces can be based on commercial market standards or concepts and solutions developed by other public agencies

[3991] In operational areas, concepts and solutions developed in NATO, or by other countries' defense forces, may be relevant

[3992] Increased standardization and reuse can also reduce the use of specialized technical equipment and, in the long term, help reduce problems with technical interoperability

[3993] It is nevertheless important that the requirement for standardization and reuse is seen in the context of the requirement that information systems must primarily meet military needs, and that the solutions must be appropriate for our Defense

[4009] INTRODUCTION The purpose of this appendix is ​​to supplement the report with professional military assessments of the Armed Forces' capabilities and limitations, as well as an analysis of given tasks in relation to the security policy situation and developments

[4010] The situation of the armed forces is characterized by the political decisions that were made in connection with St meld no. 16 (1992-93), as well as the budgets that are made available annually

[4011] Parliamentary report no. 16 called for extensive restructuring and structural changes

[4012] The structure that the Armed Forces had in the early 1990s was decided to be greatly reduced

[4013] This was to be compensated for by a qualitative increase, in order to establish a defense that was more in line with the times

[4014] Through severe operational reductions and increased appropriations, a high level of investment was to be achieved

[4015] Throughout the period 1994-98, the Armed Forces have mainly carried out the required structural changes

[4016] However, the availability of resources through the annual budgets, and an overly optimistic target for operational reductions, has not made it possible to make all the qualitative improvements that were planned

[4017] The Chief of Defence has given his advice on the development and needs of the Armed Forces through the 1996 Defence Study, and through follow-up studies of certain problem areas

[4018] The recommendation outlines a structure that is adapted to changes in the security policy picture

[4019] The recommended structure, however, is completely marginal in relation to the tasks assigned to the Armed Forces

[4020] It is therefore very vulnerable to changes, whether these are found within the security policy picture or related to access to resources

[4021] The Chief of Defence has noted that there is political will to continue both tasks and ambition

[4022] He has also pointed out what resources the Armed Forces need to achieve the aforementioned goals

[4023] However, tasks and ambition can be perceived differently, depending on the time perspective being assessed

[4024] A long-term notification applies for 4 years in the future

[4025] For the Armed Forces, this is a time perspective in which essentially the most crucial decisions about operations and development have already been made

[4026] The Chief of Defence has therefore subsequently emphasised the need for long-term planning and described the consequences of changed framework conditions

[4027] There is full agreement between the security policy assessments underlying the Long-Term Report and the Defence Study

[4028] The Armed Forces therefore continue to have a three-fold overall objective

[4029] Prevent war on Norwegian soil Provide the strongest possible resistance in the event of an attack Support society in the event of crises and disasters

[4030] This means that the Armed Forces must have a certain degree of preparedness in order to be able to demonstrate credible operational capability towards our surroundings and to ensure crisis management

[4031] At the same time, the Armed Forces must be prepared for future challenges

[4032] The prevailing security policy situation governs short-term preparedness

[4033] Long-term development provides the basis for decisions on structural development

[4034] The challenge lies in assessing the extent of long-term security policy developments in a situation that is currently characterized by peace and stability, while one must prepare for situations that could develop into crisis and, in the worst case, war

[4035] Today's perception of long-term development is characterized by uncertainty

[4036] Uncertainty is a result of the fact that changes in our surroundings are very difficult to predict, even though tendencies can be described to a certain extent

[4037] This means that the organization and structure of the Armed Forces must have the ability to meet conditions that are currently difficult to specify, which means that we must maintain the ability to meet a broad spectrum of tasks

[4038] The security policy architecture that is being developed in Europe assumes that military forces are available

[4039] Balanced military development creates a basis for finding political solutions in future conflicts

[4040] In some situations, military measures will have to be implemented, and the Armed Forces will prepare to participate in new tasks in this area

[4041] Such tasks must, to the greatest extent possible, be solved with units that are part of the national war organization

[4042] The military-strategic challenge will be found in the highlands for a long time

[4043] In the event of increased tension in other parts of our immediate area, especially in the Baltics, it will still be appropriate

[4044] and perhaps to a large extent expected, that Norway will meet possible challenges in the North in a credible manner

[4045] However, this must not reduce preparation for and participation in international crisis management outside our immediate security policy area of interest

[4046] The uncertainty in security policy developments continues to suggest that current tasks and ambitions must be continued

[4047] The capacity that must be present to meet the main task of invasion defense also constitutes the component that must at all times demonstrate credibility in relation to our surroundings

[4048] There is therefore a strong connection between the ability to provide the strongest possible resistance and to help keep us out of a war on Norwegian soil

[4049] An invasion defense capability has its most important task in preventing war from breaking out

[4050] If the main task is set at a lower level of ambition, the risk of conflict arising increases

[4051] Showing credibility is therefore a crucial factor

[4052] The military has been characterized by tight budgets for many years

[4053] Planning in recent years has been based on guidelines given in connection with Parliamentary report no

[4054] However, the report's assumptions regarding access to resources have not been met

[4055] Strong pressure on the operational side, particularly through man-year management, has also created operational limitations that must be changed urgently if irreparable harm is to be avoided

[4056] The structural changes proposed in Parliamentary report no. 16 have largely been implemented

[4057] However, the qualitative improvement falls short of the objective

[4058] The ambition of being able to respond to a possible invasion in a region of the country is already dependent on the maximum utilization of the expected warning time

[4059] The warning period is currently relatively long due to a low threat level

[4060] With a shorter warning period, it will not be possible to fulfill this ambition with today's national military capacity

[4061] The Armed Forces will continue restructuring that is considered absolutely necessary

[4062] The Armed Forces' daily operations will be carried out as rationally as possible

[4063] However, recent years have been characterized by extensive restructuring processes

[4064] Some are still ongoing, and others are being started

[4065] Such restructuring creates unrest in the organization, while at the same time drawing large resources away from the primary function

[4066] The Armed Forces' production has therefore been far below what is desirable in recent years, and the effect of the measures has not always met expectations

[4067] Extensive changes in the organization require a long time

[4068] For example, the Army's change to a new structure has resulted in approximately 400 departments being removed from the war organization

[4069] This takes time

[4070] In the context of restructuring, the Armed Forces are therefore not comparable to other organizations in society

[4071] This is due to many factors, including: Cost levels and cost developments for military equipment

[4072] Long material life and complexity

[4073] A war organization based on mobilization and conscription

[4074] Education, training and, last but not least, experience

[4075] Military equipment often has a lifespan of about 30 years

[4076] It is completely unrealistic to replace main equipment earlier, even in the event of major changes in the security policy situation or in technological developments

[4077] Larger, more expensive material acquisitions therefore create a restriction on freedom of action for several decades, which always gives us a "legacy" to take into account

[4078] Such a legacy is also present today, and will characterize the Armed Forces for a long time to come

[4079] It is therefore important that the long-term perspective is included in the assessments, and that the transition period is taken into account at all times

[4080] The possibilities for change in a defense based on mobilization depend on the frequency of rehearsal exercises

[4081] Changes in the war structure for large parts of the Defence must therefore be planned and implemented over a period where coordination with the timing of acquisitions becomes an important part

[4082] Experience shows that personnel operating simple weapons systems master this after a relatively short time

[4083] The acquisition and replacement of such systems is therefore not crucial to the ability to adapt

[4084] The pace of change is largely dependent on the personnel who will lead departments and operations

[4085] Although theoretical knowledge is an essential part of the quality of personnel, the management of military departments and operations is crucially dependent on experience

[4086] years of experience are required to lead smaller departments and 10-20 years of training and experience to serve in larger and complex departments

[4087] A core of experienced personnel is also crucial for the combat-technical and tactical exploitation of the governing sectors in the structure, such as anti-tank warfare, surface and underwater warfare, and airspace control

[4088] The described conditions therefore indicate that the Armed Forces must always have a 10-20 year horizon when factors are to be assessed and tasks are determined

[4089] Future defense must, to a greater extent than previously, be based on the whole rather than on the individual branches of defense

[4090] This is not only necessary as a result of an ever-shrinking structure

[4091] Better mobility and weapon range will enable the defense of the future to solve a broader spectrum of tasks, ranging from handling minor incidents to attacks on the countryside on a larger scale

[4092] In the longer term, however, a shrinking structure, even with the ability to perform an expanded spectrum of tasks, will mean that we will have a reduced ability to provide military presence in crisis situations

[4093] This means that the Armed Forces must have a minimum size, which the Chief of Defence has pointed out in his defence study

[4094] In connection with St report no. 16, expectations were created of a quantitatively smaller

[4095] but qualitatively better defense

[4096] There was an expectation that quality would be maintained through the acquisition of new and modern equipment

[4097] This will not be possible to achieve even if we were to achieve an annual net growth of approximately 1.5%, which is a sober calculation of the Armed Forces' needs

[4098] Procurement of only new equipment would entail an annual budget level that is approximately 3-3.5 billion higher than the current one, with a full 3 billion of this allocated to the investment portion

[4099] The future Armed Forces cannot therefore be maintained solely through new acquisitions of state-of-the-art equipment

[4100] However, modernization must continue as equipment reaches its age limit

[4101] The Armed Forces will have to address the difficult resource situation through a very conscious investment strategy, which is based on acquiring materiel in smaller series, and adapting the quality of the materiel to what is good enough for the task of the individual structural elements

[4102] The Armed Forces should take advantage of favorable purchases that may arise, including secondhand purchases, as long as this does not create an accelerating replacement rate

[4103] Within large projects, emphasis will be placed on the greatest possible degree of freedom of action in development

[4104] In certain important projects, where the equipment can be used for multiple tasks, the Armed Forces must seek to achieve the greatest possible degree of the quantitative objective

[4105] RESOURCE NEEDS The Armed Forces' short-term and long-term resource needs are set out in the Chief of Defence's recommendations

[4106] The Defence Study emphasizes short-term needs, which means the period

[4107] until the year

[4108] The short-term availability of resources is crucial for the development of the Armed Forces

[4109] A marginal increase towards the end of the period has little impact on short-term resource availability

[4110] The basis for the measures that must be implemented must be based on these conditions

[4111] The potential opportunities that a strengthened approach to resources in the longer term provides must be assessed in later analyses

[4112] The Chief of Defence has recommended that the operational side of the Defence's activities must be strengthened

[4113] This will be crucial for increasing the quality and competence of the departments

[4114] Together with other stimulating measures, this will also create new motivation and help retain crucial personnel categories

[4115] The Chief of Defence has calculated the investment requirement for the period at NOK 28.5 billion

[4116] A significantly lower resource supply than this minimum level will have to be considered very low, which will create serious consequences already in the short term

[4117] To some extent, this can be compensated for by additional funding, as the Chief of Defence has previously recommended

[4118] Additional financing improves the opportunities to implement larger projects, but complicates both the planning and budgeting processes

[4119] Therefore, clear political commitments must be given in connection with the implementation of such projects

[4120] However, additional financing in 1997-98 will not make it possible to fully achieve the objective for the important projects, which must be decided on in the coming years

[4121] In addition, the Armed Forces are already in a situation where some projects have been postponed

[4122] The short-term access to resources thus means that the Armed Forces' main task

[4123] invasion defense in a part of the country - cannot be continued for a very long time

[4124] It is difficult to pinpoint the exact timing of such a change

[4125] The main task can probably be continued into the planning period until 2006, provided that the current security policy climate continues, and provided that warning time can be fully utilized in the event of a potential crisis

[4126] It will also be necessary to assess whether our defense in the future will still be able to be balanced, or whether we will have to rely more heavily on NATO to take care of important sectors and functions for our national defense

[4127] The inability to innovate will lead to a qualitative and quantitative reduction in the structure

[4128] It is therefore highly necessary that the tasks of the Armed Forces are discussed in the context of setting budget limits

[4129] An analysis of possible future tasks will need to be carried out during the coming 4-year period

[4130] SUMMARY A certain increase in the operating budget will allow for a quality improvement in the Armed Forces' departments through a stronger emphasis on training and exercises

[4131] Similarly, sufficient financial resources will be required to ensure absolutely necessary investments

[4132] However, a low level of investment resources will mean a serious weakening of the Armed Forces, also in the short term

[4133] Although some of this can be compensated for by additional financing, large investment programs will have to be canceled, reduced or postponed

[4134] Together with the accumulated backlog from the previous period, this will eventually create an imbalanced defense

[4135] Although the security policy situation has many positive features, uncertainty is still very high

[4136] The Armed Forces must therefore continue to be able to solve a wide range of tasks in peace, crisis and, if necessary, war

[4137] The best guarantee for preserving peace is to maintain a credible invasion defense with the ability to concentrate forces in parts of the country, while simultaneously having a presence in other parts

[4138] This will also form the basis for our participation in international operations

[4139] The Chief of Defence is committed to continuing the implementation of absolutely necessary restructuring and efficiency measures

[4140] However, the restructuring measures must be weighed against the unrest they create in the organization, and the fact that restructuring measures within the war organization require a long time

[4141] For example, large and expensive equipment acquisitions will be time-consuming, while the equipment, once acquired, will have to be part of the Armed Forces' structure for 20-30 years to come

[4142] A change in facility

[4143] St report no. 22 Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period 1999-2002 of the Armed Forces must therefore have a long-term perspective, and provide freedom of action to meet several alternative development trends

[4144] A deliberate investment strategy with procurement in smaller series, and only acquiring what is good enough, will be applied

[4145] This is already embedded in the recommendations

[4146] The Chief of Defence has presented the results of his defence study

[4147] Further reductions in the war structure will reduce the overall quality of the Armed Forces and quickly lead to the Armed Forces losing their ability to solve their tasks

[4148] In light of the announced future economic framework conditions, the Chief of Defence sees a need for a broad discussion about the consequences of resource levels for the tasks

[4151] The development of the structure and activities of the Armed Forces in the years 1994-98 has been based on the goals and guidelines that were established during the Storting's consideration of Recommendation S no. 150 (1992-93), cf. St report no

[4152] The long-term report was presented to the Storting in January 1993 and was based on the recommendations of the Defence Commission of 1990, which consisted of representatives from the national parties in the Storting under the leadership of County Governor Kåre Willoch

[4153] The development and activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces in the period 1994-98 have been characterized by the most extensive restructuring that the organization has undertaken since the 1950s

[4154] Four main groups of measures have been central to the restructuring work: transition to a new war structure adaptation of the peace organization to a new war structure restructuring of the management system and organizational forms

[4155] savings in operation and maintenance

[4156] Great emphasis has been placed on the work of establishing the Armed Forces' new war structure and adapting the peacekeeping organization and its activities to it

[4157] A number of measures have been adopted and implemented to improve management and streamline operations, as well as to free up funds from operations for necessary investments in the war structure

[4158] The restructuring of the peacekeeping organization has focused on, among other things, greater concentration of operations and activities, efficient and resource-saving joint solutions, and joint localization of the activities of the defense branches and the Home Guard

[4159] At the same time, emphasis has been placed on maintaining a military presence in all parts of the country

[4160] To achieve the greatest possible effect from the restructuring, emphasis has been placed on implementing the operational cost-saving measures early in the period

[4161] Tight socio-economic conditions and a more extensive international military engagement than anticipated also reinforced the need to implement operational savings as quickly as possible

[4163] In Report No. 16 to the St., the government assumed that the difficult economic situation made it necessary to spend somewhat longer on realizing the structure than was assumed in the FK

[4164] The situation also required freedom of action to be able to change the budget level annually based on overall fiscal and security policy considerations

[4165] However, it was assumed that the budget framework during the planning period would have to be stepped up to the level

[4166] The majority of the 90s was based on maintaining the ability to defend against invasion in one part of the country

[4169] The total target for operating savings during the period was just over 1 percent on average per year

[4170] As part of the savings, a target for personnel reductions over the four-year period of 3,200 was set, but it was also emphasized that this was only a partial target that had to be seen in the context of other savings measures

[4262] Land Defence As a result of the significant changes in the war structure, the Army's peacekeeping organisation has undergone extensive reorganisation throughout the period

[4263] The reorganization has taken place through an organizational development process that affected most levels and was carried out in parallel with the work on the new war structure

[4264] The demand for efficiency and the goal of a peace organization better adapted to the needs of the war structure led to major changes at both regional and local levels

[4265] To reap the benefits of these measures, the number of district commands was reduced from 5 to 4 through the merger of District Command South and District Command West

[4266] At the same time, 15 defense districts/land defense (FDI/LF) were closed down and replaced by 14 territorial regiments and 6 divisions

[4267] The number of personnel in the regiments was significantly lower than at the FDI/LF staffs, and parts of the tasks were transferred to the district commands

[4268] At the same time, suspended departments were also closed down

[4269] Their tasks were mainly distributed between the district command staffs and the arms-specific regiments, which were retained as education and competence centers after the deployment responsibility was removed

[4270] In 1996, the Brigade in Northern Norway was disbanded as a permanent unit

[4271] The division was cadre-organized, and three educational garrisons were established

[4272] These constitute cadres for the departments in the war organization, while at the same time training personnel and producing expertise for them

[4273] As a result of the changed organization and activity in the district commands, a new workshop and warehouse organization was established in

[4274] This was designed and adapted to the needs and requirements of both the war structure and peacekeeping operations

[4275] In connection with this reorganization, and to achieve further savings, the individual departments and staff at all levels have carried out organizational development processes and implemented measures based on business analyses

[4276] The extensive restructuring of the Army's peacekeeping organization has led to the main focus of the activities being concentrated in Eastern Norway and in central Troms

[4277] In Finnmark, the border guard has been retained as a standing force

[4278] In addition, educational activities take place at the Garrison in Porsanger

[4279] In Southern and Western Norway, the Army's activities are concentrated in Evjemoen

[4280] In the rest of the country, it is the territorial regiments that constitute the Army's organizational presence

[4315] Operational activities The structure and activities of the Armed Forces have been mainly governed by the Armed Forces' war tasks

[4316] As a result of security policy developments in recent years, however, Norway has been faced with a broader spectrum of challenges

[4317] In addition to the traditional tasks such as rescue services, UN operations, and intelligence and security services, the Armed Forces have, in the period 1994-98, established units for NATO's new emergency response forces and have increasingly participated in international operations

[4318] Furthermore, the organization of the Armed Forces has become better adapted to tasks such as asserting sovereignty, crisis management and exercising authority

[4319] Personnel Personnel structure As part of the operational savings, St report no. 16 set a target for personnel reductions of a total of 6,140 man-years in the period

[4320] By the end of 1997, a reduction of 1,641 man-years had been implemented

[4321] This is approximately 26 percent of the target so far in the period

[4322] In terms of age, the reorganization has so far had an uneven effect on the officer corps

[4323] The attrition rate among younger professional officers in the 25-37 age group has been high in all branches of defense

[4324] Combined with declining applications to the military academies, this has led to significant imbalances in the command structure

[4325] As a result, the number of temporarily employed officers is higher than planned

[4326] A lack of personnel with the right expertise has caused problems for some departments

[4327] More younger officers than expected have resigned or applied for leave from the Armed Forces

[4328] Therefore, the practice of graduate stimulating measures, such as study support and support for starting one's own business, has generally been very strict

[4329] The most commonly used measures to stimulate retirement have been early retirement and retirement on reduced salary

[4330] Early retirement, along with support for studies, has been the most widely used measures on the civil side

[4331] During this period, much effort has been made to increase the quality of the Armed Forces' education and training

[4333] The service periods for conscripts are differentiated, mainly between 6 and 12 months of service

[4334] At the same time, the system of continuous service has been expanded, particularly in the Army

[4335] In 1998, nearly 80 percent of the personnel in the Army performed their entire initial service at one and the same duty station

[4336] A number of measures have also been implemented to improve the quality of the repeat service

[4365] This tool facilitates comprehensive follow-up of all aspects from the early phase of the project until the equipment is introduced into the organization

[4366] Material management High material investments can increase operating expenses over time

[4367] Streamlining operations is therefore a prerequisite for maintaining a high investment rate and securing the necessary funds for operating the new equipment

[4368] This has placed great demands on efficient management of materials

[4369] A separate project (LOGSTRAT) has been established to improve the Armed Forces' logistics processes, including materiel procurement, supply and storage, transport, maintenance, scrapping and disposal of all types of materiel

[4370] The Armed Forces have achieved rationalization gains as a result of more efficient materiel management, but the process has taken longer than expected, and it has proven difficult to measure the gains accurately

[4425] THE TRANSFORMATION PROCESS It has been and is a major challenge to implement the extensive restructuring of the Armed Forces that followed from the framework and guidelines that the Storting approved in the spring

[4426] For many employees in the Norwegian Defence Force and for many local communities and municipalities, the restructuring has had significant consequences

[4427] Military units, often with solid historical roots, have been disbanded, merged with others or relocated

[4428] According to the Ministry's assessment, the restructuring of the Armed Forces has been carried out in a responsible and planned manner

[4429] An impressive effort has been made at all levels of the organization, and good collaborative relationships have been developed with affected local communities

[4430] The Ministry of Defence has emphasized that the transition should take place in transparency and in close cooperation between the ministry, professional military management at various levels, personnel organizations and affected local and regional authorities

[4431] The Ministry has also placed emphasis on reducing the consequences for the affected parties through information activities, personnel policy measures and support measures that facilitate alternative business development in the municipalities that are most affected

[4432] The Ministry has the overall and coordinating responsibility for all public relations and information activities in the Armed Forces

[4433] Information has been important in creating understanding of the Armed Forces' restructuring and in mitigating negative reactions to the Armed Forces' reduced activities in various local communities

[4434] A separate information strategy has been prepared for the restructuring

[4435] Information to personnel and their organizations has followed the framework established in the Main Agreement with the Adaptation Agreement for the Armed Forces

[4436] Understanding the municipalities' information needs has also been crucial for progress and cooperation in the restructuring process

[4437] Local military commanders have played a key role in this context, both in relation to the personnel and their organizations, and to local authorities

[4438] The Ministry has also carried out information trips to affected regions in advance of the government's submission of reorganization proposals to the Storting

[4439] In addition, all proposals have been discussed with the personnel organizations at local, regional and central levels

[4440] The information strategy was evaluated in the summer

[4441] The target groups for the survey were employees and leaders in the Armed Forces, politicians and the administration in affected municipalities, and the media

[4442] The results indicate that the information has contributed to a greater understanding of the transition among these groups

[4443] The restructuring has reduced the need for personnel in the Defence Force

[4444] While the goals for the restructuring have been set, the Ministry has placed emphasis on implementing the process with people in focus and with the greatest possible safety for the personnel affected

[4445] The personnel policy guidelines that are the basis for the restructuring process are described in St meld no

[4446] In order to be able to provide advice and guidance to each redundant employee, it was crucial to put a good support system in place across the country as early as possible

[4447] By establishing the Resource Organization for the Redundant, the central and regional support apparatus was put in place

[4448] However, it has been crucial that the restructuring work has also been followed up locally

[4449] It has been a key goal for the Armed Forces to create the best possible conditions for those who become redundant to find new jobs

[4450] Therefore, a number of measures were implemented to stimulate retirement and mobility among personnel, including by facilitating continuing and further education, so that redundant personnel gain enhanced competence for work outside the Defence Forces

[4451] Arrangements have also been made for loans, rentals or purchases of vacant premises from the Armed Forces, and possibly also the transfer of materiel and equipment to establish one's own business

[4452] Support measures for affected municipalities

[4453] The significant restructuring of the Norwegian Armed Forces' organization and activities that is now being implemented will have consequences for a large number of municipalities and many local communities

[4454] To mitigate the negative consequences for affected local communities, the Ministry of Defence, together with the Ministry of Local Government and Labour, has implemented various measures to stimulate alternative industrial development

[4455] The most significant contribution in this context has been the implementation of our own restructuring. St. report no

[4456] Main guidelines for the activities and development of the Armed Forces in the period

[4457] According to the municipalities that have participated in the restructuring programs, 650 jobs have been maintained and created during this three-year period; 250 of these are new jobs, of which 52 are filled by redundant personnel from the Armed Forces

[4458] Participating municipalities expect an additional 650 jobs as a result of the program in the coming years

[4459] In addition, there are other factors that the municipalities find positive in connection with the implementation of the restructuring program

[4460] This includes general competence development within business development, network building both internally in the municipality and externally with other municipalities, access to commercial areas through the release of Defence property, buildings and facilities, and increased emphasis on work with alternative business development in the municipalities

[4461] To further mitigate the negative effects of the Armed Forces' downsizing, the Ministry of Defence has placed considerable emphasis on facilitating the restructuring efforts in the municipalities

[4462] This has been achieved, among other things, through the use of the Armed Forces' freed resources (personnel, property, buildings and facilities, and materiel) as a supplement to the financial support

[4463] These are collectively included in the planning of specific projects anchored in the municipalities' business plans

[4464] In connection with the ongoing restructuring of the Armed Forces, the Storting has authorized the King to transfer properties, buildings and facilities that the Armed Forces no longer need to municipalities or redundant personnel in the Armed Forces in connection with the utilization of the establishments for business development

[4465] This is intended to mitigate the negative effects when defense-related activities in municipalities are discontinued and to help ensure that redundant personnel in the Armed Forces can find alternative jobs in the local community

[4466] The Ministry has made it an essential requirement that both the municipalities and the Armed Forces use resources to create jobs for redundant defence personnel

[4467] This must therefore be part of the planning that takes place locally in collaboration between the municipality, department, the Resource Organization and the Armed Forces Building Service
